307.report:
Independent review of PR #307, three rounds, head e19078b (earlier rounds 57d5440 and cce4117), base stage. The reviewer ran in a separate context and never edited the implementation.

ROUND 1 (57d5440). Product side clean: no references to any removed name anywhere in *.py/*.iss/*.spec/*.ps1/*.bat, verified both by grep and by an AST scan of SetupWizard for attributes that are read but never assigned. Step indices confirmed: STEPS and renderers line up one to one, LAST=5, the Finish gate moved correctly from step 5 to step 4, and only the Multilogin gate was lost, which was the point. Re-running setup on a configured machine was verified live rather than by test: a .env seeded with MULTILOGIN_AUTOMATION_TOKEN_A in both quoted and exported forms survived two calls to apply_machine_configuration; mutations that put the key back into env_values, or made merge_env drop unknown keys, both went red. The build is untouched: acl_windows.spec never listed a removed name, and the wizard no longer imports src.web at all.

One real defect: test_setup_is_six_steps_and_the_screens_match_them promised to match the step list against the renderer list but asserted block.count("self._") == len(STEPS), which is a count. Swapping self._identity with self._files left the suite green — the wizard would have shown "Your name" above the file pickers and parsed the stats workbook on the wrong step, silently.

Two notes: the Readiness list showed four green ticks and read as "all done" with the Multilogin warning as a separate paragraph below; and Finish said "press Connect" while the Accounts screen carries three buttons containing that word, the right one being "Connect Multilogin".

ROUND 2 (cce4117). The counting test now compares names in order. Eight ways of desynchronising the two lists were tried — removing an element, adding one, swapping non-adjacent pairs, reordering STEPS against renderers, reordering both consistently, a cyclic shift, and duplicating a renderer — all red. The button name is fixed and matches _account_map_add.html line 70.

New blind spots found in the replacement test: it read the source as text, so commenting the line out left it green over an empty screen (the neighbouring phrase test had the same illness), and it did not check colour at all, so turning the yellow marker green passed. A four-line stand was demonstrated: _readiness runs without Tk given system_checks, configuration, stats_path, creatives_path and a stubbed _text.

ROUND 3 (e19078b). Both blind spots closed. The _draw stand was compared against a real tkinter render under root.withdraw(): Readiness matched 10 widgets to 10 rows with identical text, colour and order; Finish matched all three labels, the stand simply not seeing the Button. Commenting out either phrase, turning the marker green, replacing the bullet with a tick, deleting the row, moving it above the checks, and putting the green Safety line back under the yellow one all go red.

Two tails, both non-blocking and both recorded as follow-up work. The adjacency assertion names one specific line at one specific offset: a different green line directly below, or the Safety line one row further down, still pass. And the stand cannot see the Tk Button on Finish — a typo in a Tk option (text= written as txet=) raises TclError in a real render but leaves the suite green; this was equally true before this change, so it is an open gap rather than a regression.

Test runs, all three rounds: 196 passed, 1 skipped, and one pre-existing unrelated failure in tests/test_team_library.py, which is ACL-1289 (tests reach into the real target library) and floats between tests of that file between runs.

Verdict: e19078b may be merged into stage.

ROUND 4 (f7476f2). The tracker refused to record the approval of e19078b because the working branch was two commits behind main; both were merges of this branch own earlier PR (#304 into stage, then stage into main via #306). Current main was merged into the branch. The merge is purely procedural and was verified as such rather than assumed: the tree SHA of f7476f2 is identical to the tree SHA of e19078b (6024920a), so git diff between the two heads is empty and the working tree did not change by a single byte. main is now an ancestor of the head. The one real risk of such a merge was checked explicitly: tests/test_the_installer_signs_in_to_multilogin.py still exists in main and this branch deletes it, so the merge could have resurrected it; it did not, the deletion survived and still stands in the diff against main. Nothing foreign arrived: everything main touched under packaging/windows since the branch base was this same task four commits. Test runs repeat the approved head exactly. The approval of e19078b therefore carries over to f7476f2 without reservation.

Independent review of PR #312 (ACL-1311 Team access), three rounds; the reviewer ran in a separate context and never edited the implementation. Head e95ef60, base stage 723652e.

ROUND 1 (9505d6e). Approved, no blocking findings. Security of the token route verified through ASGI: GET/HEAD/OPTIONS 405, Origin null 403, cross-site Referer 403, Origin localhost other port + Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site 403, foreign Host (evil.example, localhost.evil.example, 127.0.0.1.nip.io) 400 — none return the token. A local process without Origin gets it, which is not new: it can read the machine .env anyway. No token in logs at DEBUG, Sentry has send_default_pii=False, token never lands in markup or DOM, including the real Clipboard API branch checked on http://127.0.0.1. sign_in is called only from /multilogin-signin; the leftover builder panel is dead code and hits the server refusal. A dead token never shows as connected. Findings: the setup wizard still told buyers to sign in with email and password; 11 of 32 mutations survived, the real gaps being copy from the wrong slot, next_step for expired, Copy on a dead token, false 'copied' when execCommand fails, flag case, the +60 s margin, 401 without exp called expired; a refused Clipboard API showed a raw browser error; deployment notes missing (restart after setting the flag, flag absent from .env.example).

ROUND 2 (a5ee726). All seven author mutations red, none passing by coincidence; the clipboard fallback on 127.0.0.1 works after a refused writeText with and without permissions; packaging/windows/tests 45 OK. Four remaining non-blocking gaps: the fallback after a refused Clipboard API was not exercised because the test page ran on http://acl.test (no secure context); the 'not accepted' label untested; a dead 'expired if readable' branch; the Readiness wizard text untested.

ROUND 3 (e95ef60). All four closed. The new test runs the page on http://127.0.0.1:9 (isSecureContext true) with a refused writeText; removing the fallback or replacing it with an empty catch turns it red. 8 of 9 delta mutations red; the survivor (always copying through the field) is not a gap, copying still works. 338.report: Approved. The change to _discover_owned_debug_port.norm (src/fb_ads_rpa/browser.py:1542-1554) is correct and fixes the root cause of the 2026-09-27 stage incident. On this machine (Python 3.14.3), os.path.realpath of a real GetShortPathNameW name in a temp dir returns the long path, identical to realpath of the long form. A missing tail under a short prefix still expands the existing prefix. A junction resolves to its target, so the same profile can't look like two different ones, and two different directories can't collapse into one. Quotes are stripped before realpath. Live psutil on this machine shows every Mimic --user-data-dir fully in 8.3 form (C:\Users\EVGENI~1\mlx\profiles\B18D03~1\3EF7F4~1\5D508A~1). The stage log confirms the chain: at 08:45 the profiles were reattached, but ownership failed on the path compare, so _mark_robot_profile was never called. At 12:33 connect_over_cdp timed out and _robot_profile returned False, so the job stopped with no_automation_port (browser.py:2076-2080). The earlier 1443 unowned_port stop at 08:45:47 has the same cause (browser.py:2062-2065). The hand-opened-profile protection is unchanged: a process still has to own a LISTEN socket on its debug port and accept CDP. The new test file, plus the hand-opened, spend-regression and two-minute suites, pass: 67 passed in a detached worktree. Both short-path tests fail against base 47152af, so they do guard the regression. Non-blocking notes: (1) Four substring helpers build needles from the long path and its leaf, and those needles never match 8.3 command lines: _kill_chrome_for_user_data_dir (browser.py:145-184), _profile_process_running (1450-1476), _discover_debug_port (1478-1531) and _profile_pids (1840-1866). They still work only because the main Mimic process carries the profile id in --client-session-id (4/4 live main processes). That is an undocumented MLX detail, so a realpath-based compare there would be sturdier. (2) After this fix, a robot profile whose CDP connect times out now goes to _start_via_mlx_api (browser.py:2090). That may return the same hung port, so the live acceptance criterion should be checked on a real run. (3) realpath costs about 1 ms per call here, roughly 40 ms per check across 38 Mimic processes. That is acceptable, and a raw-string equality short-circuit or cache would remove it. The except fallback is effectively dead. For an unreachable UNC path, realpath returned instantly with an odd C:\host\... result, which is harmless because profiles are local. (4) account_spend._dir_spellings (src/analysis_agent/account_spend.py:525) is now a redundant workaround; dashboard track can simplify it later. Follow-up: the only change after the reviewed head 2d1a42d is a merge of work/main (19fadc3); the tree is byte-identical (f4d92c5361dcf21dbc9b2c4fc18cb32fe508360e), so the approval carries over unchanged.

It fixes a Windows-CI flake in the stopped_profile_page fixture: connect_over_cdp could win the race against Chromium opening its first tab, so `attached.contexts[0].pages[0]` raised IndexError. The new code waits up to 10s for ctx.pages to be populated and falls back to `ctx.new_page()` only if the wait times out; either branch yields a real page in the live attached context, and the fixture still calls page.set_content(...) and asserts md._page_responsive(page, 3.0) is True before closing, so the assertion is unchanged and unweakened — the new_page fallback is exercised only in the rare case the original tab genuinely never appears, and it still tests a real, responsive page. Ran tests/test_a_stopped_profile_never_spins_the_robot.py in the C:\acl-1327 worktree via C:/fb_agents/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest: first run showed 1 failed / 6 passed, but the single failure was in a different test (test_the_probe_and_the_waits_on_a_stopped_profile_return_at_once), on an unrelated CPU-rate timing assertion (`rate > 0.25 * base`) untouched by this delta; a clean rerun immediately after passed 7/7, confirming ambient machine noise rather than a regression from this change. Worktree left untouched (read-only, no edits or commits).

343.report: Round 3 re-review in a fresh detached worktree (C:/acl-rev343c, removed after review). All 8 PR test files pass one at a time (symlink tests skip x2+2 for lack of privilege): meta_campaign_agent 7+2skip, account-header 2, asset-export 6, click-recorder 5, creative-file 4+2skip, dead-multilogin-panel 6, scrubber-shapes 50, scrubber-never-hangs 16. acl_scan_secrets.py: clean. THE ROUND-2 BLOCKER IS FIXED: the quoted-value pattern is now (?:\\.|(?!\4)[^\\\n])* with an optional closing quote group (\4)?. Independently fuzzed every regex in run_telemetry.py (scrub/_SCRUB alternatives and scrub_diag/_hides_dict_value) via subprocess-isolated adversarial inputs: unterminated quotes with 28..50000 backslash pairs, truncated JSON-escaped Windows paths, FB-style escaped-slash HTML fragments, 100KB and 4MB (the real MAX_HTML_BYTES ceiling) unterminated payloads, long runs of hyphen/dot/space/camelCase-hump separators (up to 50000 reps), 2000-5000 keys in one blob, and a 100KB random adversarial mix. All completed in well under the test suite's own 0.5s/case ceiling; the 4MB worst case (realistic page_capture.scrub_html ceiling) took 1.8s, linear. Mutation-tested: (a) reintroducing the exact round-2-flagged ambiguous alternation (?:\\.|(?!\4).)* alone did NOT reintroduce the blowup, because the newly-added optional closing-quote group means the overall match can never fail at that position, so the engine never backtracks into the ambiguous alternation regardless of exclusivity -- informational only, not a defect, the shipped pattern keeps both defenses; (b) narrowing _KEY_SEP back to '_?' correctly broke 6 of the round-2 hyphen/dot/space/header tests, confirming that fix is real and covered. S01 dead-panel JS: no remaining raw cid/instance concatenation into onclick/oninput JS text or unescaped id/CSS-selector attributes in that block; the two round-2-flagged spots (oninput filters at old report.html:8548/8681) now pass cid via data-cid+this.dataset, ids go through aclEscHtml, and the two querySelector call sites use CSS.escape(cid); the two getElementById/.id-property sites that still string-concat cid are safe (DOM property/exact-id-lookup, not markup or eval'd JS text). NON-BLOCKING (new, previously unflagged): (1) the round-2 suffix-matching widening of _BARE_KEY_START to treat '_' as a valid boundary (not just non-word chars) means the STRING-based scrub() -- unlike the dict-based scrub_diag/_hides_dict_value, which is deliberately bool/int/None-aware and is tested for this -- has no way to tell a boolean/counter flag from a real secret, so free text like 'has_token: True', 'hasToken: true', 'is_token=False' gets redacted to 'has_token: <hidden>' etc; this reaches Sentry/telemetry whenever such text appears inside a diag string value (verified: scrub_diag({'note': 'has_token: True, alive: False'}) hides the flag). Loses diagnostic value, does not leak a secret. The code's own comment and test only promise this stays visible for actual dict keys. (2) the quoted-key form's prefix is bounded to 40 lazy characters (by design, for linear time); a key whose junk/organization-specific prefix before the recognized secret suffix exceeds ~40-46 chars is NOT redacted at all -- e.g. '{"' + 'x'*45 + '_refresh_token":"SECRET"}' leaks the value in full. Narrow/contrived in practice (no such key names exist in this codebase today) but a real false negative if it ever occurs; worth a comment noting the tradeoff or raising the bound modestly. Neither blocks: no realistic new secret-leak path was found, the intended threat model (real credential field names in this codebase and common header spellings) is covered, and the P1 ReDoS is conclusively closed. | Coordinator note: head moved bde9473->768df3a by a merge of work/main only; tree unchanged (889bc37), verified with git rev-parse HEAD^{tree} before and after.

The merged tree passed 637 affected tests (31 test files plus packaging test_machine_config), run headless with an empty ACL_LIBRARY_*. GitHub reports the PR as CONFLICTING.

## Findings
1. HIGH, src/acl_sentry.py:167-169 (pre-existing, but now load-bearing), used by src/fb_ads_rpa/run_summary.py:565 and scripts/run_summaries.py:130.
   `init()` sets the `machine` and `machine_id` tags with `sentry_sdk.set_tag`, which writes to the isolation scope of whichever thread calls init first. The summary is sent from a new daemon thread. Once init has run, the threading integration forks that new thread's scope from the spawning job thread, which never had the tags. Reproduced with real sentry_sdk 2.69.1 and a fake transport: a job thread sends two summaries. The first carries machine=Dan and machine_id; the second has no machine or machine_id tag at all. Only `manager` survives, because it is added in before_send. `run_summaries.machines()` groups by `machine`, so every summary after the first lands in "unknown". That breaks the per-machine table (AC 4 and the live acceptance "lists both machines").
   Fix: set machine/machine_id in `_before_send`, as is done for manager, or on `sentry_sdk.get_global_scope()`. Add a test that sends two summaries from a non-init thread and asserts the machine tag.
2. MEDIUM, scripts/run_summaries.py:45,84. Grouping is keyed on the `machine` label. The wizard now writes ACL_MACHINE_LABEL = manager name, and telemetry_sync.machine_identity uses that as the machine label (the test asserts machine == "Dan"). Two computers of the same manager, or a renamed label, merge into one row, and the hostname is no longer visible. Fix: add machine_id to FIELDS and group by it, with the label shown.
3. LOW, src/fb_ads_rpa/ads_manager_flow.py:2339-2509. The summary is sent only on the recorded_flow normal return. If run_recorded_campaign_flow or _goto_campaigns raises something other than ProfileStop, no summary is sent (the job exception still goes to Sentry). The llm_agent and recipe_player engines send no summary. This is acceptable because recorded_flow is the default, but it is worth a note.
4. LOW, src/fb_ads_rpa/run_summary.py:527. The campaign name is not passed through scrub_text. It still goes through before_send scrub_diag, so this matches the owner decision, but an e-mail or act_ id typed into a campaign name would only be caught by the generic scrubber.
5. INFO: the live acceptance (owner and tester machines in Sentry, --from-sentry listing both) is still open by design.

## Checks done
- Safety: no Publish path, no browser or Multilogin changes, and no visible windows. Sending happens in a daemon thread and swallows all errors. The switch ACL_SENTRY_RUN_SUMMARY=0 works, and conftest defaults it to off.
- Ids, URLs, tokens and e-mails are scrubbed; names are sent, as the owner decided.
- User-facing text (wizard, dashboard, errors) is in English.
- Mutation spot-checks on tests/test_run_summary_reaches_sentry.py: dropping the manager tag, the URL/e-mail scrub, the switch, background sending, or do-not-publish each makes tests fail. The tests are real.
- Profile-stop path: the publisher clears the current run per campaign, so a stop at connection does not pick up the previous campaign's steps.

## Verdict: request-changes

## Findings

1. MEDIUM, src/web/app.py:275 vs 3405-3411 / 3461 (with 1527): the panel and the save path seed from different reports.
   `_render_report` replaces the report with `report_for_period(...)` (app.py:1527; month-to-date by default), and `_build_goals_view` seeds from that period report.
   `_goal_countries_now()`, used by GET/POST /goals, seeds from `get_cached_report()`, which covers the whole workbook.
   Effect: someone who sees e.g. Chile and Mexico at 10 edits Chile, and the saved goals also pick up every country where they had spend at any time in the workbook. They never saw those rows.
   The seeded strip also changes with the date picker: pick a single day and the goals become only that day's countries.
   This breaks the PR's own claim ("Те же страны, что видит панель"; "first edit keeps the starting countries") and the Issue's intent of a shown seed that the first edit persists.
   Fix: use one period-independent source for both, for example seed `_build_goals_view` from the unscoped cached report's countries (or the same helper that POST uses). Add a test where the period report and the full report differ.
2. LOW, src/web/app.py:3405-3411: `_goal_countries_now()` calls `get_cached_report()` synchronously inside async handlers. On a cache miss (workbook mtime changed, or the selected CM is not cached) it rebuilds the whole report (Excel + GSheet) and blocks the event loop on a goals save.
3. LOW, src/web/app.py:3461 / `_my_goal_countries`: the seed always uses the selected CM's report plus this machine's whole account map. When a team lead edits another CM (`who` != selected), or on a shared machine, the map countries are not that person's. This is an edge case, and the default UI posts `_gCm` = the report's CM.

# Independent review — PR #511 (ACL-1495, Issue #495)

Reviewer-R1495X (rev_r1495x_1003). Implementer: Worker-L1495K.
Head debd55aec2806b8f6bf76dec700c52f8d32341ca (tree d1d69e1cfb5dd055356271db8af21664b6fe4df3); base work/stage 91b0a27fcf03db57f303dc3d85805801f4e1b703.

## Verdict: APPROVED

## Code review of config.paths.machine_file_lock
- No lost update: the process-local RLock plus the cross-process lock wrap the whole read-modify-write in `_transaction()`. Writes go through `_atomic_write` / `paths._replace_when_free`. Proven: 3- and 16-process runs leave no update missing.
- EDEADLK is retried, with a bound. Each attempt is a non-blocking `LK_NBLCK` / `LOCK_NB`. EACCES, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, EDEADLK and EINTR count as busy. Any other OSError is raised. The pause is jittered and grows from 5 ms to 100 ms. The wait stops at the deadline (`_LOCK_TIMEOUT` 120 s) with TimeoutError. There is no unbounded wait.
- The lock file is created atomically: `os.open(O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_BINARY)` in one call, and it is never written. The test confirms the file stays 0 bytes.
- Windows semantics:
  - `lseek(0)` runs before both lock and unlock, so the region is always the same: byte 0, length 1. Locking past EOF is legal.
  - Unlock happens in the inner `finally`, and `os.close` in the outer one.
  - The region matches the old `LK_LOCK` byte 0, so old and new processes still exclude each other during a mixed-version upgrade.
- Non-Windows: `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` raises BlockingIOError (EWOULDBLOCK), which is in the retry set. This was checked by reading only. CI runs on windows-latest, so the POSIX branch is not run anywhere.
- hidden_accounts and targeting_registry both call the helper. The old inline LK_LOCK blocks are fully removed. `LK_LOCK` now appears in these files only in comments.

## Findings (none blocking)
1. Minor: the tests do not guard against a missing `_unlock`. With `_unlock` replaced by `pass`, all 44 tests still pass, because closing the handle releases the lock. The code is correct as written; this is only a gap in the safety net.
2. Minor: if the body raises and `_unlock` also raises, the original exception is masked. This is unlikely, and the old code had the same behaviour.
3. Follow-up, already declared out of scope: `src/acl_log.py`, `ad_text_registry.py` and `team_library.py` still use the 10 x 1 s `LK_LOCK` pattern and can hit the same EDEADLK under load.
4. Note: callers do not catch the TimeoutError raised after 120 s. A dashboard request would return an error instead of hanging, which is the intended trade-off.

## Evidence
- Affected tests on head: test_file_lock_races, test_hidden_accounts_review, test_targeting_registry, test_machine_paths and test_bench_catalogue gave 60 passed. `scripts/acl_scan_secrets.py` is clean.
- New tests run against the old code (work/stage): 8 of 8 failed.
  - The EDEADLK repro fails with `OSError [Errno 36] Resource deadlock avoided`.
  - The first-use repro fails with `PermissionError(13)`.
- Mutations, each restored afterwards:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| EDEADLK removed from the retry set | 3 failed |
| `b"0"` written into the lock file | 3 failed |
| Deadline removed | 2 failed (bounded-wait tests) |
| `LK_NBLCK` changed to `LK_LOCK` | 2 failed |

The wait is bounded at 120 s, and EDEADLK, EACCES and EAGAIN are retried. The lock is always taken in the same order (thread lock, then OS lock), so there is no new deadlock. I checked that an exception inside `ar._transaction()` releases the lock: a later acquire succeeds.
2. Timeout, checked with `_LOCK_TIMEOUT=0.3` and the lock held:
   - `acl_log` raises `JournalWriteError`, which is correct.

- Client: `AMAP_OPEN_INFLIGHT` is held until the original request settles, and the button stays disabled until then. In adv2 case S3 the button stays disabled while the first open is in flight and comes back once it settles. The test catches M12 (button re-enabled early).

**N1: resolved.** The test now asserts `status == "Active"` and that the row is not `local_only`, so M1 is caught.

**N2: mostly resolved.** The helper bodies are tested: M7 (`amapPrefillSelect`) and M8 (`amapOwnerHint`) are caught. The call sites are not: M7b (prefill call removed) and M8b (hint call removed from the Accounts row) survive.

**N3: owner's decision, not a finding.** The Home account map shows whole-account workbook numbers (all CMs) for an account connected here. This is today's behaviour and is kept on purpose. The report and period numbers (`my_cm`, `_period_key`, cache `_cm_key`) stay filtered by buyer.

**N4: resolved.**
- `/mlx-profile-open` waits at most `OPEN_WAIT_S = 70` s, using `wait_for(shield(task))`.
- After that it answers 409 `{timeout: true}` with the English message.
- The thread is not cancelled, and nothing is killed or restarted.
- M11 is caught.

**N6: resolved.** After a timeout, the message stays up for 6 s before the reload or the `/account-links` call, with or without a country. M15 is caught. Harness case 4 and adv2 S1 confirm it with country=Chile.

## Coordinator checks

### Q2. Is the single-flight lock always released?
I checked this with a scratch probe, rev1588/lock_probe.py.

- **On exception:** the task completes with the exception and the done-callback pops the entry. The next open runs and returns 200. The exception itself still returns a plain 500, as before. `open_profile_for_automation` catches almost everything internally.
- **On the server timeout:** the 70 s answer does not release the lock. This is by design, because the thread is still opening.
  - A second request answers `already_opening`.
  - Once the thread returns, the entry is popped and the next open runs.
- **A finished task can never block:** the guard is `existing is not None and not existing.done()`, so it holds even if the callback failed. That makes M14 (callback pop removed) an equivalent, harmless mutation.
- **If the open thread hangs for good:**
  - Connect for that one profile keeps answering "already being opened" until `serve.py` restarts, and one to_thread worker stays occupied.
  - Other profiles are unaffected. So are the map-row "open profile" route, reads and MLX Desktop.
  - Closing the profile window in Multilogin should break the CDP call and release the lock. I did not verify this live.
  - Suggested non-blocking follow-up: limit the lock's age, or make the 409 message say what to do after N minutes.

### Q3. Can the 70 s server answer make the client save a wrong row?
No. In adv2 case S1 the server answers `{ok:false, timeout:true}` with instance B.
- `_openTimedOut` is set and the probe is skipped.
- The patch carries the found profile_id `pS`, the folder `fdS` (from `_details`) and `multilogin_instance` "B". The ad account is empty because the user left it empty.
- With country=Chile, `/account-links` is sent after the 6 s message. Without a country, the page reloads.
- The row is upserted by name, so there is no duplicate.

When the server answers `already_opening` (adv2 S2), the flow continues as an ordinary open failure. The probe is attach-only (`read_ad_account` uses `_attach_only` and never launches). The row is saved with the right profile, folder and instance.

M13 (the client ignoring `d.timeout`) survives, because the harness only exercises the client's own 75 s timeout. Even then the row is not wrong: the attach-only probe runs, and the same correct row is saved.

### Q4. Merge-tree against the current work/stage
Clean against 6c6c5d60.

### Q5. CI
All checks are green on fe694c26. No tracker-link rerun was needed.

## Non-blocking notes
1. **The harness passes when a case hangs.** It has no completion check. If a case awaits a promise that never settles, node exits 0 and the assertions after it never run. That is why M9 (client in-flight guard removed) passes. Fix: add an `exit` hook that fails if the IIFE did not finish, as rev1588/adv2.cjs does.
2. **Some paths have no test.** M7b and M8b (call sites) and M13 (server `timeout` flag handled in the client) survive.
3. **The `already_opening` message conflicts with the flow.** The message says to wait, but Connect goes on to the name prompt and saves. The saved row is correct; only the UX is inconsistent.
4. **The lock has no age limit.** See Q2.
5. **The lock covers only `/mlx-profile-open`.** `/account-spend/open-profile` (`open_for_automation`, serialized by account) could still run alongside a hung Connect open of the same profile. That route existed before this PR.

  - Accounts: the row comes from the sheet and is not `local_only`.

4. **Range end clamp.** The mutant is caught by test_range_end_beyond_file_is_clamped.

### New code checked
- **`fresh=True` in the publish-time callers** (publish.py, dashboard_publisher.py, enrich_draft.py).
  - It passes `recheck=True`, which skips the 5 s throttle and calls `_dirs_changed`. That is one `os.stat` per indexed directory, with no listing and no file stats. A full walk happens only if a directory mtime changed, or the 60 s safety net is due.
  - Cost per ad is D stats, done under the index lock. That is acceptable at publish time, and much cheaper than the old rglob per ad.
  - Semantics: a duplicate added inside the window now gives AmbiguousCreativeError at publish. A mutant ignoring `fresh` is caught by test_fresh_lookup_sees_a_duplicate_added_inside_the_throttle_window.
  - Callers' exception handling is unchanged.
- **The 60 s full rebuild.**
  - It is lazy: it runs only inside a lookup, so an idle dashboard does no work.
  - It is thread-safe: it runs under `_index_lock` and swaps in a new immutable snapshot, and readers that already hold the old snapshot keep using it safely.
  - Who pays: the first lookup after the 60 s mark builds synchronously. That is a preview thread from the 4-thread pool (never the event loop) or a publish caller. Lookups that arrive during the build wait on the lock for one tree walk; the request that triggered it still pays the walk itself.
  - This is strictly better than before the PR, where every lookup paid a full rglob. The mutant removing it is caught by test_full_rebuild_safety_net_finds_file_when_dir_mtime_never_changes.
- **N stale callers cause one rebuild.** Rebuild happens only if `snap is seen`, so a snapshot another thread already replaced is reused. An evicted root (`None`) still rebuilds. The mutant dropping the identity check is caught by test_concurrent_stale_callers_cause_a_single_rebuild.
- **`bytes=-0` gives 416** with `Content-Range: bytes */size`, and the middleware keeps it no-store. The `n == 0` branch is redundant: without it, `start = size > end` also gives 416, so that mutant survives by equivalence. That is harmless.

- The 60 s rebuild, and a mtime-triggered rebuild, run inside the global lock. During the build, other preview lookups and publish lookups wait for one tree walk (off the loop). On a very large tree, consider building outside the lock and swapping the snapshot under it (double-checked), so readers keep serving from the old snapshot.
- Round-1 notes still apply but are minor: a `bytes=` parse that is lenient (`+3`, `1_0`), and one `os.stat` on the loop in the Range path.

- **Only one write path.** `set_note()` is the only writer; `grep` finds no other writer of `account_notes.json` in `src`, `scripts` or `config`. It reads through `_load_strict()` inside `_transaction()`. The tolerant `load()` is now used only for rendering (the map view and `GET`).

- **Lock timeout.** `machine_file_lock` raises `TimeoutError` (a subclass of `OSError`) before anything is read. The endpoint answers 500, the file is untouched, and the editor stays open with "save failed".
- **Unreadable file.** Any `OSError` other than `FileNotFoundError` propagates, so the save is refused with 500 and the bytes are unchanged (tested). A failing `path.replace(backup)`, for example on a sharing violation, is also an `OSError`, so the save is refused and nothing is lost.
- **Corrupt file.** A JSON error, a `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError` subclass), a wrong root, or `notes` not being a dict all cause the original bytes to be moved to `account_notes.json.corrupt-<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>` before the new file is written. Tests cover both a broken JSON and a wrong root, and both assert the backup's content.
- **Residual risks (non-blocking):**
  - The backup name has one-second resolution, and `Path.replace` overwrites. Two separate corruptions within the same second would lose the first backup. This needs two hand corruptions in one second, so it is negligible. Adding a uuid or nanoseconds would close it.
  - Inside a valid dict, non-string values such as `{"A": 5}` are silently dropped on the next save. They can only come from a hand edit.
- **Visibility to the user (non-blocking).** A corrupt file is not surfaced:
  - The map silently shows "add note" in every row.
  - After the first save, the old content sits in `.corrupt-*`, but the response, the UI and the log say nothing.
  - An unreadable file likewise renders empty, and its saves show "save failed".

  No data is lost any more, but the manager cannot tell that their notes still exist on disk. Suggestion for a follow-up: log a warning and return `{"recovered": "<backup name>"}` so the editor can show "previous notes file was damaged and kept as …". Alternatively, show a hint on the map when `load()` hits a parse error.

- **Repeat click while saving.** The `mousedown` capture runs `close()`, which sets `saving = 1` and starts the POST. The following click on a cell hits `open()`, which returns immediately. **Verdict: approved.** I found no blocking issues.

## Round-2 blockers

### R2-B1: a job waiting on the stopped robot held a queue slot — fixed
`_run_job_inner` now calls `_wait_for_stopped_robot` before `_slots.acquire`. The waiting job is not in the slot queue's waiting list or running list, so it holds no slot and does not block other accounts.

**1-slot repro.** I re-ran my round-2 scenario on this head, with one slot:
- Job A on Doc19 hangs and is abandoned.
- Job B on Doc19b (same profile) shows `hold=stopped_robot`.
- Job C on KLD now runs to `done`.

The PR adds the same case as `test_with_one_slot_a_stopped_profile_does_not_block_other_accounts`.

I also extended the repro. After A's thread exits, B then waits for C's ACL-1603 kept window, with the reason `override_full`. That is correct ACL-1603 behaviour, not a leak.

**Slot hand-back.** This covers a job that was granted a slot while A was being abandoned. After the grant, the job checks `_stopped_robot_on`; if it is true, it calls `_slots.release(job_id)` and loops back to the wait.
- **No double release.** `release` is an idempotent `pop` of the job's own id. A cancel during the re-wait or the re-acquire returns before the `try`/`finally`, so no claim or release happens twice. The abandoned job's own slot is settled once, through `_claim_slot`.
- **No leak.** After the hand-back the job is in neither `_running` nor `_waiting`. The test `test_a_job_queued_before_the_abandon_gives_its_slot_back` checks this.
- **No race.** A same-profile job can only be granted a slot after the abandoned job's slot has been freed, and that happens only in `_abandon_job`. `_abandon_job` sets `abandoned` and `profile_key` under `_jobs_lock` before calling `release`. So the check after the grant always sees the abandon. A job that slips past the check would still block on the real profile lock.
- **Kept windows (ACL-1603).** A grant calls `_reuse_kept(profile)`, which drops any kept-window entry for that profile, so a hand-back could in principle discard one. It cannot happen here: profile P cannot have a kept window at that point. Same-profile jobs are serialised, and the abandoned job's slot was released, not kept. The extra `_grants[P]` increment only makes `account_spend._publish_touched` more conservative, so a read will not close the profile.

### R2-B2: merge conflict — fixed
`git merge-tree --write-tree work/stage HEAD` against the current stage (84ff7d0a) is clean and gives the same tree as the head (d0d136b2).

#624 had not landed when I checked. I simulated its head 99d58c3a on top of this one: `report.html` auto-merges, and only `docs/system/CHANGELOG.md` conflicts again. That is a mechanical resolution for whichever PR merges second, not a code issue.

## Other round-2 items
- **Profile key cached on the job.** It is computed outside `_jobs_lock` and stored together with `abandoned`. If the key cannot be resolved it is None and never matches, so the job falls back to the real profile lock, which is safe.
- **Limits are documented** in the CHANGELOG.

# Independent review, round 2 (delta): PR #639 (ACL-1637, same video on several ads)

- Reviewer: Reviewer-R1637K, session rev_r1637k_1006. This was read-only and no pytest was run locally; it relies on CI logs and reasoning.
- Implementer: Worker-M1637V
- Head: 517cc3571729b0eaf20bedcbd4769264f510ae30. The review fixes are a1c67a67 and 415218cf; 517cc357 merges work/stage 39a9cb1b, which includes ACL-1630.
- Base: work/stage 39a9cb1b9606562edff740157e095924cba26e58. It is an ancestor of the head.
- Tree: b4b2f465827490551b4d7736b9a62f49eb31cab3. The merge with stage is clean and equals the head tree.
- Round 1 (head 533d7dfd) was request-changes for H1 (CI red), M1 (failed files re-uploaded), M2 (hang not addressed), L1 and L2.

## Verdict: APPROVED

All round-1 blocking findings are resolved and CI is green on the exact head. The new findings are low severity and non-blocking (suggested follow-ups).

## Round-1 findings: status

| # | Round 1 | Round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | Source-window test failed in CI | **Fixed.** The AST test checks the `if reuse_only:` branch: `_reuse_known_copy` comes before `_close_creative_setup_modal`, the last statement is `return`, there is no upload call, and `LIBRARY_HAS_NO_COPY` is present. It also checks `known is False` maps to `library_pick_left_selection`. It passes in CI shard 2. |
| M1 | Every known-failed file was re-uploaded | **Fixed.** `_failed_uploads` is now a dict of reasons. `upload_failure_allows_reupload` uses the allow-list `_NAVIGATION_WHYS` plus `file_not_landed`, and everything else is denied. In the refused-media branch, the reason is now set *before* it is remembered. There are 3 new tests (5 cases). |
| M2 | 573ab 19-minute hang not addressed | **Addressed.** The CHANGELOG states it is outside the creative-upload path and names the ACL-1614 owner. The coordinator says it is filed as ACL-1641. |
| L1 | `file_not_landed`/`wizard_not_opened` not named in summary | **Fixed.** Both are in `creative_soft_fail` and in `PER_AD_DETAIL`, and the parametrized test asserts BLOCKING and an "Ad media - " title for both. |
| L2 | Five mutation gaps | **Closed.** There is one test per gap: budget before round 2, empty or oversized cache file, dirty pick at wrapper level, media-on-ad checked before re-upload (3 probes), and `known is False` naming. |

## Answers to the coordinator's four checks

### 1. Is every allow-listed reason truly "the file never reached Meta"?
**Mostly, but not strictly. This is finding N1/N2 below.**

The six `_NAVIGATION_WHYS` are `wizard_not_opened`, `upload_button_missing`, `media_step_locked`, `media_step_unreachable`, `media_step_covered` and `media_picker_loading`. `upload_ad_creative` sets all of them only *before* `_note_file_offered()` (meta_dom.py ~12313). So within a single attempt they really mean the file was not offered.

**N1 (Low): a navigation reason from attempt 2 can mask a file that was offered in attempt 1.**
- A first upload runs with `attempts=2`. `_upload_why_tls.offered` is sticky for the whole wrapper call, but the reason is reset per attempt.
- Example: attempt 1 offers the file and fails with `media_not_on_ad`, `file_not_landed`, `wizard_left_open` or a stall followed by a reload. Attempt 2 then fails with `wizard_not_opened` or `media_picker_loading`.
- The give-up path then runs `_remember_upload_failed` because the file was offered. It stores the *navigation* reason, which allows a re-upload on later ads.
- The terminal "Meta saw it" cases are not affected, because they return inside attempt 1 with their own reason: refused media, crop, and page closed or unreadable.
- Cost: one bounded upload attempt per later ad, for a file that Meta did not reject on content.
- Suggested follow-up: in `_remember_upload_failed`, when `_file_was_offered()` and the reason is in `_NAVIGATION_WHYS`, store a non-allowed reason. Alternatively, keep the first post-offer reason of the call.

**N2 (Low, wording): `file_not_landed` means "no library tile within ~30 s × 3 feeds", not "never reached Meta".**
- The upload loop sets it even when an attempt recorded `uploading: true` or `state: "progress"` (bytes were flowing).
- It is not a content refusal, because a refusal is detected separately and denied. The re-upload decision is therefore defensible.
- The CHANGELOG and comments ("never reached Meta") overstate it. "Meta did not reject the file" would be accurate.

### 2. Is there a default-deny for unknown reasons?
**Yes.**
- `upload_failure_allows_reupload` returns True only if the file has no failure memo, or if its stored reason is in `_REUPLOAD_OK_WHYS`.
- `""` (no reason; `_remember_upload_failed` stores `last_upload_why() or ""`) and any unknown or future reason are denied.
- Tested for `crop_wizard_stuck`, `upload_failed_unnamed`, `page_closed` and `media_refused_on_ad`. `""` is not tested explicitly (gap G2).

### 3. Did the side-effect test edits weaken their checks?
- **`test_media_step_reached_or_named::test_each_ads_upload_failure_carries_its_own_reason`:** `"ad_creative_upload" in flow` became `any(r.startswith("ad_creative_upload") ...)`.
  - The row is now the named `ad_creative_upload:wizard_not_opened - ...`. The per-ad telemetry note checks for ad1 and ad2 are unchanged, and so is the Sentry reason check.
  - This is very slightly looser: a prefix match instead of an exact row. It could have asserted the exact named row. Acceptable, and not a weakening of the property under test (each ad keeps its own reason).
- **`test_closed_browser_stops_the_ads_cleanly::test_failures_before_the_stop_are_kept`:** it only adds `_set_upload_why(None)` before the run, which is test isolation. All assertions are unchanged.
  - In production the wrapper resets the reason at the start of every ad, so the leak exists only between tests. Not weakened.
- The `quiet` fixtures in both ACL-1637 test files now also reset the reason on teardown. That is isolation only.

### 4. Is the new failure_policy entry still blocking?
**Yes.**

# Review of PR #658 (ACL-1628): three flaky CI tests

Reviewer: Reviewer-R1628Q (rev_r1628q_1006). Implementer: Worker-S1628A.

## Verdict: APPROVED

Only four test files change. No product code changes. `git merge-tree --write-tree work/stage HEAD` is clean (d0f42b1f). CI is green on all 13 checks, with no reruns.

## (3) Stopped-profile rate check (MIN_RATE_WINDOW_S = 0.25)
Method: a scratch wrapper around `md._wait_objective_dialog`, run against the real stopped-Chromium fixture. The same mutations ran on the old stage version for comparison.
- **GIL-holding spin that replaces the wait** (pure-C `sum(range())` loop, then return "gone"). This is the ACL-1320 failure shape.
  - 0.3 s: the new test failed 3/3 times on reruns (rate about 0.05–0.25 of base). It passed once out of 4, and the old test has the same noise because the assertion is identical.
  - 3 s: both old and new fail.
  - 0.1 s: the old test fails, the new one passes. This is the accepted cost: the spin is bounded below 0.25 s, and the time bound (< 6 s) still holds.
- **Pure-Python spin, or a loop of failing Playwright calls**: 0.3 s and 3 s pass in both old and new. A Python loop gives up the GIL every 5 ms, so the neighbour thread keeps about 0.4–0.5 of its rate. This gap existed before the PR; it is not a weakening.
- **GIL spin placed before the real ~1 s wait** (0.3 s and 3 s): passes in both old and new, because the 1 s wait dilutes the rate. Also a gap that existed before the PR.

Conclusion: the PR only stops checking the rate on windows shorter than 0.25 s. The flake had exactly that shape: rate 0.0 over a return of about 0.1 ms. The time bound still proves the fast return. No meaningful guard is lost.

## (2) Drawer lost/cancelled: poll held until both posts are made
Mutations to `halt()` in report.html:
- **No `batch.uncertain`**: the drawer test fails on [missing], and the harness fails too.
- **The halt call replaced by a plain settle**: the drawer test fails on [missing].
- **`halt()` also settles already-submitted jobs** (survival broken): the drawer test passes, but `tests/test_publishing_everything_at_once.py` (builder_publish_all_harness.cjs) fails.
- **`halt()` no longer stops previews in flight**: the drawer test passes, the harness fails.

Both survival and the in-flight halt are therefore still guarded, by the node harness. The drawer test never actually proved survival: in the missing case both jobs return 404. The old test only "covered" the in-flight halt through the race that caused the flake.

## (1) Builder publish selected
- Firing `input` on the asset field matches what a real user does: the field has `oninput="cbUpdateName(...)"`. `cbAddSlot` sets the asset and then calls `cbUpdateName`, and I found no product path that sets the asset without updating the name. The product names campaigns correctly.
- Mutation: the checkbox aria-label pinned to "untitled campaign" makes the test fail. Good.
- Mutation: the `oninput` handler removed from the asset field, so the name only follows through the 350 ms drawer check. The test passes 3/3. `expect(...).to_have_attribute` waits up to 5 s, so the test no longer pins how quickly the label follows the name. The old test did not pin it either: its bare `.value` never fired `input`.
- Product note (low severity, not caused by the PR): the drawer card name and checkbox aria-label come from a full tree paint. `cbDrawerRefreshIndicators` does not repaint names, so between an edit and the next paint (at most 350 ms plus the preview fetch) the card can show the old name. A real user typing usually triggers a paint, so I am not raising this as a bug.

# Review of PR #671 (ACL-1572, issue #572): round 3 (delta)

Reviewer-R1572N, session rev_r1572n_1007. This was an independent, read-only review. I ran no local browser tests and killed no processes.

- **Head:** 7271d3e3490be95da68928d4d4486465b53700fa. The delta reviewed is 2c55f59b..7271d3e3.
- **Base:** work/stage eab2d0e1258195d07726c56c041c79e1f7a95f0c. Stage moved since round 2, but only with ACL-1649, a CI-workflow change that does not touch meta_dom or retry_policy. The merge-base is still 0fa66af6.
- **Head tree:** bc0e245d5eee424182c1d14456e998331e713291.
- **Merge with work/stage:** `git merge-tree --write-tree work/stage HEAD` is clean and gives tree 5edc2b504e2bdd1a33a1573bcd62a08c168e47e7.

## Verdict: approved

The silent-corruption risk is closed on the engine that installed builds run. The follow-ups are listed below and are not blocking.

How it is closed:

- **No keyboard opener.** `_open_conversion_menu_via_keyboard` is gone. Nothing in the conversion step presses a key on the page.
- **One name check for the whole step.**
  - `_NameGuard` reads the name once, at the outermost entry. Nested guards do not take a new baseline.
  - `conversion_name_changed` is sticky until the next outer guard.
  - Both `_pick_website_from_open_menu` and `select_conversion_location_website` return False if the name changed.
- **Recorded flow** (`run_recorded_campaign_flow`):
  - It wraps the pick in `_NameGuard`. A rename returns `conversion_website_name_changed`.
  - That step is in BLOCKING_REVIEW_STEPS and NON_RETRYABLE_FLOW_STEPS, has BLOCKING severity in failure_policy, and adds its reason to `result.error` and `blocking_failures`.
  - The campaign is not replayed.
- **The recorded flow is the shipped engine.**
  - `.env.example` and `packaging/windows/machine_config.py` set `FB_RPA_ENGINE=recorded_flow`.
  - `config/paths.py` turns a blank value into recorded_flow.
  - The diagnostics have a `safety_engine_ok` check.
- **The reason no longer contains ad set names** (`NAME_CHANGED_REASON`).

## Answers to the coordinator's checks

### 1. Can a name change still end in a passing step?

| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| Recorded flow (production) | **No.** Blocked, never replayed, reason in `result.error`. |
| `select_conversion_location_website` called once | **No.** Its retries share one baseline. Tested by `test_select_conversion_location_website_blocks_a_name_changed_during_its_retries`. |
| AdsManagerFlow legacy wizard (FB_RPA_ENGINE not recorded_flow) | **Yes.** See below. |
| recipe_player | **Yes.** See below. |
| ai_website_recovery (`try_deterministic_website`) | Has its own baseline; it is not called anywhere in src. |

AdsManagerFlow legacy wizard, `_select_conversion_location_website` (ads_manager_flow.py:1824):

- When `select_conversion_location_website` returns False, the method falls back to the unguarded `_click_first` selector path. It then calls `diagnose_and_recover` (line 1883), which calls `select_conversion_location_website` again.
- That call opens a new outer guard and takes the renamed value as its baseline, so it can pass as `..._selector` or `..._recovered`.
- For the first call (line 2238), `_fill_ad_set_name` runs afterwards (line 2253) and overwrites the name. The second call (line 2257) runs after the name fill, so a rename there would stick.

recipe_player:

- `_run_delegated("conversion_location")` calls `select_conversion_location_website` twice, and each call is a separate outer guard. The second call takes a new baseline.

Both of these engines are opt-in and not shipped. **Follow-up:** put the step-level `_NameGuard` (or a per-campaign baseline) around `AdsManagerFlow._select_conversion_location_website` and `RecipePlayer._run_delegated`, or make `name_changed` sticky per campaign.

### 2. Can `_conv_tls` leak between campaigns on the same thread?

**No, in the recorded flow.**

- `reason`, `name_changed` and `baseline` are reset on every outer guard entry.
- `_open_state()` is cleared at the start of every pick.
- A successful `_done` clears `reason`.
- The flow reads `last_conversion_failure_reason()` only for `conversion_website` and `conversion_website_verify`, and both are produced after a guarded pick in the same campaign.
- `conversion_name_changed` and `_ensure_conversion_menu_open` are called only inside a guard. The stale `baseline` and `name_changed` left over after a step are never read outside one.
- `__exit__` runs on exceptions too, including job cancel, so `guard_active` cannot stick.
- Concurrent accounts in separate job threads are isolated, as `test_the_reason_is_kept_per_thread` shows.
- Test hygiene: the autouse fixture resets the `_conv_tls` fields.

### 3. Without Enter, can the menu still open from the Doc21 capture state?

**On the bench, yes. Live, it is not shown.**

- Bench: in `test_the_focus_in_the_name_field_is_released_before_the_trigger_is_pressed`, the trigger cannot be focused, mousedown is preventDefault'ed, and the script opener is off. The click opens the menu only after the explicit blur. The control test without the blur stays shut. `dead_click` mode, where a real mouse click is ignored and the script click opens, passes through `_open_conversion_menu_via_js`.
- Live: the evidence is weaker than the PR's framing.
  - In 87d43d6202af and 162a95a64776, the old flow had already CDP-clicked the `tabindex=0` trigger about 16 times. A real mousedown would have moved focus out of the name field.
  - So focus alone does not explain why every click failed, unless the CDP clicks never reached the page. In that case the only new lever is the one script `el.click()`, which the old code effectively never sent to the trigger: its JS strategy runs only when the locator finds nothing.
  - The name input's `aria-expanded=true` appears with no `role=listbox` in the DOM. The captures are truncated, though.
  - Whether Meta's combobox opens on a script click is unverified. No open-menu capture exists.
  - The issue's Live acceptance criterion stays open. That is fine for merge, but a live Doc21 run is needed before closing #572.

## Findings (most severe first)

1. **LOW-MEDIUM (follow-up).** Non-default engines (legacy AdsManagerFlow, recipe_player) can still pass after a rename, because each separate `select_conversion_location_website` call takes a new baseline (see check 1). They are not reachable in installed builds.
2. **LOW.** The recorded-flow branch has no behavioural test.   - if the tree cannot be read (-1), it raises, and the caller's `except` records `fail_adN_create`;

# Review of PR #692 (ACL-1691), round 3 (delta)

- Reviewer: Reviewer-R1691T, session rev_r1691t_1007. This is an independent, read-only review.
- Implementer: Worker-K1691H
- Head: 74743093af9185ad9d59383849c59207859e1d14. This is a merge commit with parents 707383c0 and work/stage 87273788.
- Base (work/stage): 872737889a376fbcdab4333c3a526055f06bbf2b. The merge-base is the same commit.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree work/stage <head>`: fa34dcf85c6dcc0358df1c27a2957eeb6282f2fc, with **no conflicts**.

## Verdict: approved

F5, F6, F7 and F8 from round 2 are resolved. The merge resolution keeps ACL-1641's behavior. The per-thread state is cleared and read at the right moments. The single retry cannot produce a duplicate from the blocked call. Two notes below are non-blocking.

## 1. Merge resolution vs work/stage

- `git diff work/stage HEAD -- src/` contains only this PR's changes. `_adopt_shell_or_recreate` is byte-identical to stage, and all of ACL-1641's other edits (step budget and so on) are present.
- At the call site, the non-block path is stage's path exactly:

  ```
  created = create_additional_ad(...)
  if not created and recover_stuck_page(...): created = create_additional_ad(...)
  if not created: created = _adopt_shell_or_recreate(page, adset_name, shells_before)
  ```

  The only additions on this path are the local `block` / `retried` assignments and the label `adN_create` (with `:<reason>` only when a block reason exists). For non-block failures the label stays `adN_create`, the same as stage.
- After a block whose recover-recreate then fails in an ordinary way, `block` becomes "" again, so the code goes through ACL-1641's adopt path. That is correct, because the second call may have clicked.

## 2. Per-thread state

- `_create_tls = threading.local()` follows the same pattern as `_conv_tls` and `_upload_diag_tls`. `last_create_block()` defaults to "".
- `_set_create_block("")` is the first statement of `create_additional_ad`, before any page call. So no exception path can leave a stale reason from an earlier call.
- The reason is set only on the block, right before `_diag` and `return False`.
- The caller reads `last_create_block()` immediately after each of its own `create_additional_ad` calls: the first call, the recover re-create, and the block retry. Nothing that can call `create_additional_ad` runs in between. The skip check and the label use the same local.
- **Leak from ad N into ad N+1 on the same thread:** not possible. Every read follows a call that cleared the state first.
- **Leak across threads:** not possible, because the state is thread-local. The two-thread test checks both directions: A's block is not wiped by B, and B's ordinary failure is not labelled with A's block and still adopts.

## 3. Single retry: duplicate risk

The retry runs only if all three of these hold:

- `block` is set;
- `not retried`, meaning `recover_stuck_page` did not already re-create;
- `0 <= _tree_new_ad_shells(page) <= max(shells_before, 0)`.

A block implies no click in that call:

- The block is reached only when `surface_clicked` is False. That requires `_click_adset_action_menu` to have found no element, so its DOM click never ran.
- The wake did not draw the button, and the wake only moves the mouse.
- The coordinate `mouse.click` sits after the block's `return`.

So the blocked call cannot have produced a shell. The guard also covers a late shell from earlier activity: if the count grew, there is no retry. An unreadable tree (-1) also means no retry.

Two shells from the retried Create (the Doc20 case) is a separate, pre-existing risk. The caller's existing check (`shells_after - shells_before > 1`, giving `extra_ad_shell`) still handles it.

If the retry itself fails in an ordinary way, there is no adopt on the block branch. The ad fails as `adN_create`. Any late shell is handled the same way it is on stage after its single recreate.

The guard is sound on paper, but untested (N1).

## Notes (non-blocking)

- **N1 (test gap).**
  - The flow fixture fixes `_tree_new_ad_shells` to 0 and `recover_stuck_page` to False.
  - So removing the shell-count guard (M23) or the `not retried` condition (M22) passes every test.

- **N2 (label).**
  - On the non-block path, `_adopt_shell_or_recreate` may itself call `create_additional_ad`, and that call may block.
  - The local `block` is then stale (""), so the label lacks `:adset_action_menu_not_shown`.

- **It cannot reach another profile.** The browser session belongs to the Playwright `Browser` connected over that profile's own `cdp_url` (one Chrome process and port per Multilogin profile). `Target.getTargets` lists only that browser's targets, so another profile's window or tab is not visible to it.

  - nothing is closed, and the target is never sent a renderer call.

Criteria: (1) retry once on transport error, already-stopped on retry = stopped - met and tested (ConnectionError and ReadTimeout parametrized, plus already-stopped 500 on retry); (2) the raised error names the primary failure and not the tail 404 - met, test asserts exception type/text and the address are in the message, '404' is not, and only the primary was asked; (3) tail kept only for a primary 404 - met, test asserts 4 calls with no repeat of the primary. 1026.title: Update ACL shared workflow and task lifecycle support
1026.body:
## Description
Adopt the shared Task Tracker and Master Repo support that distinguishes a task's workflow category from an executor's confirmed activity. ACL should show honest work time and explain movement into and out of Review using the common implementation, so an occupied slot or an old Review label cannot look like continuous work.

## Specifications
### Context and expected behavior
- Owner authorized the common fix and ACL adoption on 2026-10-19. The shared implementation belongs to [TT-174](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/174); shared rules and exact export/pin support belong to [MR-65](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/65).
- Current ACL selects Master 1.5.3 `6f7e9416e68c66484a3b6c0213eab24847005b8f` and Tracker 3.7.1 `be87599d1b5e625058bbddc33c35bda86687b5bf`. Implementation waits for accepted exact compatible upstream revisions.
- Workflow status, recorded ownership and confirmed executor activity remain separate. An old or silent executor is unknown, never automatically stopped or released. Work time must not grow through unconfirmed activity or waiting intervals. Existing Review history must remain available through the common Tracker projection.

### Scope and constraints
- Update compatible exact standard/engine pins and the maintained exported helpers/generated selected guide using the native upgrade procedure, plus truthful ACL instructions and the guarded operator adapter only if necessary for shared client integration.
- Use the shared executor activity contract. Do not create ACL-specific heartbeat/presence logic or a detached process that confirms an idle executor.
- Preserve descriptor2, package profile and target, draft adoption, active execution3 with 5/5/5 limits, process1, Stage disabled with permanent stage retained, absent optional context/completion/retry/native-CI policies, all required checks, 71 historical aliases and +1000 task numbering, historical receipts and genuine ownership.
- No campaign runtime changes, live advertising actions, state migration, clearing another owner's claim, or package run without the real supported admission/delivery route.
- Fulfilled upstream prerequisite: [TT-174](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/174), native Merged; published Tracker [v3.7.3](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/releases/tag/v3.7.3) at `5d0a915c9fdb8dea4e3aded38beaa8dd1a024ecc`, verified 2026-10-20.
- Fulfilled upstream prerequisite: [MR-65](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/65), closed/Merged; published Master [v1.5.4](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/releases/tag/v1.5.4) at `10da6de5b496a21e10188f2df63bef1f0254afbf`, verified 2026-10-20.
- Original planning prerequisite: actual reviewed revisions had to be verified before implementation; external references were unresolved until inspection. Both are now verified above. The shared reader/service is published; ACL consumer adoption remains this task.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ACL pins accepted compatible shared revisions and generated/portable artifacts match their actual upstream manifests.
- [ ] ACL's guarded adapter reaches shared activity operations without bypassing adoption checks; any required integration change has focused behavioral coverage.
- [ ] Selected guide and local instructions describe confirmed activity, waiting and unknown activity truthfully, preserving workflow categories and existing ownership/review/delivery controls.
- [ ] Existing ACL policy choices, IDs, historical evidence and unrelated product/runtime files remain unchanged.
- [ ] Separate non-implementing source review, applicable checks and genuine existing frozen-batch admission/delivery are completed or their concrete remaining blocker is recorded accurately.
- [ ] Actual source adoption and reader/writer/publication verification are recorded separately; source pins alone are never reported as live activation.

### Implementation and verification
- Route is the existing ordinary approval-only source PR into main, independent source review, Approved, authorized Coordinator's frozen batch with independent combined review, required exact checks and the genuine package completion condition. Policy/config/helper edits cannot use the instruction-only shortcut.
- Worker: Worker-ACT174A, an actual isolated agent session. Coordinator: Coordinator-ACT174, actual session recorded privately. Acquire a real implementation claim only when upstream dependencies and actual repository capacity permit implementation.
- Check exact export/descriptor consistency and focused ACL adapter/adoption regression tests first; preserve required hosted Linux/Windows/installer checks. Review existing unchanged evidence before requesting more checks.

### Handoff
- 2026-10-19: planned dependent adoption; no implementation claim, PR, code edit, migration or delivery yet. Exact upstream accepted pins are pending from the owning Coordinator. Duplicate search found no current task owning this shared executor activity adoption; older tracking/adoption tasks retain their original scope.

- 2026-10-20: fulfilled upstream prerequisites verified at the exact published pair above. Original requirements, acceptance criteria and historical planning remain preserved. No implementation claim yet at this checkpoint.

### Latest owner amendment — global process/product separation — 2026-10-20
- The owner explicitly required process updates to be delivered separately from the product for every repository and installation profile, then instructed implementation. This task continues the original activity-support adoption and now adopts that global process-only completion boundary as part of the same shared-support upgrade.
- For this proven isolated process outcome, the latest instruction supersedes the earlier plan's assumption that an ACL Windows installer publication is necessary merely because ACL uses the package profile. The original plan and criteria above remain historical evidence. Actual product/runtime/installation changes and explicit product-publication requests retain their original package checks and delivery; this task requests none of them.
- Published support verified: Master [v1.6.0](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/releases/tag/v1.6.0) at `6cbc2bbfd5df76fc2f1ad6f285d33a45dd5ff504`, compatible Tracker [v3.8.0](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/releases/tag/v3.8.0) at `9c3ad4deec6b3596d5ef48400430b126155012dd`. Shared work: [TT-177](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/177) and [MR-68](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/68). These publication prerequisites are verified independently of each Issue's broader lifecycle; no active external dependency marker is being inferred as a local task.
- The genuine Coordinator returned the old Approved source for author revision using the maintained command before this amendment. Prior `ca9a650` source approval and all original history remain preserved; they do not approve this changed scope or future head. Keep original PR1027, author, branch and isolated worktree. All unrelated owners and five source-review reservations remain untouched.
- Preserve all non-pin descriptor fields exactly as actual main, including its historical explanatory exception; put current support explanations in repository prose. Tracker config, layout, product/build/install/update/release inputs, all policies/targets/checks, IDs and prior receipts remain unchanged. Inspect actual imports and indirect build inputs, not directory names alone.

- No consumer product delivery request, Windows publication, migration or foreign-owner recovery is authorized or created here. The earlier automatically rejected Windows publication is not resumed. Process completion requires the supported exact admitted-main proof; unknown or mixed content stays unfinished.

### Additional acceptance for the owner amendment

### Latest owner amendment — one cumulative ACL update — 2026-10-20

Reuse ACL-2026 / source PR1027 and preserve the complete original requirements, decisions, reviews and handoffs; no duplicate adoption task is needed.

- Include the accumulated common process changes: truthful owner-confirmed activity and native task history; process/product delivery separation; phase-preserving explicit Pause/Resume support; approved waiting work in Delivery as Ready for integration; genuine Needs fixes in Backlog and actually owned Fixing in In Progress; fresh independent Review after corrections; continuation of the already owner-selected task set under actual capacity/admission, with existing explicit pause/new-work/integration decisions. Retain five categories and configured native keys. The shared header cleanup is already delivered by the shared reader.
- Current actual ACLmain is259ae7f (full SHA recorded with final source evidence). Assess its unrelated completed product changes; preserve them in the candidate. Use the maintained three-way upgrade and genuine pristine baseline, reconciling local instruction overlaps intentionally. Preserve descriptor2, all non-pin descriptor fields, config/layout/policies, package target/checks, 5/5/5 capacities, no Stage with permanent stage history, absent optional context/completion/retry/CI policies, 71 aliases/+1000 IDs, all receipts and real owners. No unrelated product change or global skill installation.
- The old source is held by a genuine independent Reviewer. That actual run must return it through supported ownership before the original Worker reclaims and edits. Record a fresh source handoff/review on the complete cumulative scope. Ordinary approval-only source, authorized frozen integration, independent combined review, all applicable checks, exact process-support and final-main proof remain required.
- This is a process-only update if and only if the exact immutable full diff plus independent product-isolation review proves it. No product-release request, unchanged Windows installer publication or application rollout is requested, and the earlier rejected product publication is not resumed. Mixed/unknown product effects must be investigated rather than waived.
- New pins install Pause support but do not activate outer8. Inspect real service/every-writer/adapter/CI/recovery readiness and actual live ownership. Do not stop/transfer foreign work merely to manufacture idleness, rewrite shared state or pretend old Todo-moving stops preserve phase. If genuine owners or unknown readiness block activation, retain the exact remaining boundary visibly pending rather than calling source merge live activation. No new scheduler or automatic restart.

### Additional acceptance for the cumulative update

- [ ] ACL owner/operator guidance accurately describes the accumulated lifecycle, correction, activity and process-only delivery behavior, including genuine capacity/manual boundaries and conditional live Pause activation.

1026.title: Update ACL shared workflow and task lifecycle support
1026.body:
## Description
Adopt the shared Task Tracker and Master Repo support that distinguishes a task's workflow category from an executor's confirmed activity. ACL should show honest work time and explain movement into and out of Review using the common implementation, so an occupied slot or an old Review label cannot look like continuous work.

## Specifications
### Context and expected behavior
- Owner authorized the common fix and ACL adoption on 2026-10-19. The shared implementation belongs to [TT-174](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/174); shared rules and exact export/pin support belong to [MR-65](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/65).
- Current ACL selects Master 1.5.3 `6f7e9416e68c66484a3b6c0213eab24847005b8f` and Tracker 3.7.1 `be87599d1b5e625058bbddc33c35bda86687b5bf`. Implementation waits for accepted exact compatible upstream revisions.
- Workflow status, recorded ownership and confirmed executor activity remain separate. An old or silent executor is unknown, never automatically stopped or released. Work time must not grow through unconfirmed activity or waiting intervals. Existing Review history must remain available through the common Tracker projection.

### Scope and constraints
- Update compatible exact standard/engine pins and the maintained exported helpers/generated selected guide using the native upgrade procedure, plus truthful ACL instructions and the guarded operator adapter only if necessary for shared client integration.
- Use the shared executor activity contract. Do not create ACL-specific heartbeat/presence logic or a detached process that confirms an idle executor.
- Preserve descriptor2, package profile and target, draft adoption, active execution3 with 5/5/5 limits, process1, Stage disabled with permanent stage retained, absent optional context/completion/retry/native-CI policies, all required checks, 71 historical aliases and +1000 task numbering, historical receipts and genuine ownership.
- No campaign runtime changes, live advertising actions, state migration, clearing another owner's claim, or package run without the real supported admission/delivery route.
- Fulfilled upstream prerequisite: [TT-174](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/174), native Merged; published Tracker [v3.7.3](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/releases/tag/v3.7.3) at `5d0a915c9fdb8dea4e3aded38beaa8dd1a024ecc`, verified 2026-10-20.
- Fulfilled upstream prerequisite: [MR-65](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/65), closed/Merged; published Master [v1.5.4](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/releases/tag/v1.5.4) at `10da6de5b496a21e10188f2df63bef1f0254afbf`, verified 2026-10-20.
- Original planning prerequisite: actual reviewed revisions had to be verified before implementation; external references were unresolved until inspection. Both are now verified above. The shared reader/service is published; ACL consumer adoption remains this task.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ACL pins accepted compatible shared revisions and generated/portable artifacts match their actual upstream manifests.
- [ ] ACL's guarded adapter reaches shared activity operations without bypassing adoption checks; any required integration change has focused behavioral coverage.
- [ ] Selected guide and local instructions describe confirmed activity, waiting and unknown activity truthfully, preserving workflow categories and existing ownership/review/delivery controls.
- [ ] Existing ACL policy choices, IDs, historical evidence and unrelated product/runtime files remain unchanged.
- [ ] Separate non-implementing source review, applicable checks and genuine existing frozen-batch admission/delivery are completed or their concrete remaining blocker is recorded accurately.
- [ ] Actual source adoption and reader/writer/publication verification are recorded separately; source pins alone are never reported as live activation.

### Implementation and verification
- Route is the existing ordinary approval-only source PR into main, independent source review, Approved, authorized Coordinator's frozen batch with independent combined review, required exact checks and the genuine package completion condition. Policy/config/helper edits cannot use the instruction-only shortcut.
- Worker: Worker-ACT174A, an actual isolated agent session. Coordinator: Coordinator-ACT174, actual session recorded privately. Acquire a real implementation claim only when upstream dependencies and actual repository capacity permit implementation.
- Check exact export/descriptor consistency and focused ACL adapter/adoption regression tests first; preserve required hosted Linux/Windows/installer checks. Review existing unchanged evidence before requesting more checks.

### Handoff
- 2026-10-19: planned dependent adoption; no implementation claim, PR, code edit, migration or delivery yet. Exact upstream accepted pins are pending from the owning Coordinator. Duplicate search found no current task owning this shared executor activity adoption; older tracking/adoption tasks retain their original scope.

- 2026-10-20: fulfilled upstream prerequisites verified at the exact published pair above. Original requirements, acceptance criteria and historical planning remain preserved. No implementation claim yet at this checkpoint.

### Latest owner amendment — global process/product separation — 2026-10-20
- The owner explicitly required process updates to be delivered separately from the product for every repository and installation profile, then instructed implementation. This task continues the original activity-support adoption and now adopts that global process-only completion boundary as part of the same shared-support upgrade.
- For this proven isolated process outcome, the latest instruction supersedes the earlier plan's assumption that an ACL Windows installer publication is necessary merely because ACL uses the package profile. The original plan and criteria above remain historical evidence. Actual product/runtime/installation changes and explicit product-publication requests retain their original package checks and delivery; this task requests none of them.

- No consumer product delivery request, Windows publication, migration or foreign-owner recovery is authorized or created here. The earlier automatically rejected Windows publication is not resumed. ### Additional acceptance for the owner amendment

### Latest owner amendment — one cumulative ACL update — 2026-10-20

The owner explicitly instructed proceeding with one ACL update task after reviewing the completed shared releases. This replaces the earlier defer-ACL restriction for this task. Reuse ACL-2026 / source PR1027 and preserve the complete original requirements, decisions, reviews and handoffs; no duplicate adoption task is needed.

- Adopt the complete actually published Master1.7.2, exactmain4f148cbbbc2c9c65a7fdebba9b37551f91566e04 (https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/releases/tag/v1.7.2), and its compatible Tracker3.9.2 exactmain3d32586d72e4621f70d56d35f1e199a19fa13b00 (https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/releases/tag/v3.9.2). The shared snapshot service is already deployed at3d32586d72e4621f70d56d35f1e199a19fa13b00. These facts are prerequisites, not ACL adoption proof.
- Include the accumulated common process changes: truthful owner-confirmed activity and native task history; process/product delivery separation; phase-preserving explicit Pause/Resume support; approved waiting work in Delivery as Ready for integration; genuine Needs fixes in Backlog and actually owned Fixing in In Progress; fresh independent Review after corrections; continuation of the already owner-selected task set under actual capacity/admission, with existing explicit pause/new-work/integration decisions. Retain five categories and configured native keys. The shared header cleanup is already delivered by the shared reader.
- Current actual ACLmain is259ae7f (full SHA recorded with final source evidence). Assess its unrelated completed product changes; preserve them in the candidate. Use the maintained three-way upgrade and genuine pristine baseline, reconciling local instruction overlaps intentionally. Preserve descriptor2, all non-pin descriptor fields, config/layout/policies, package target/checks, 5/5/5 capacities, no Stage with permanent stage history, absent optional context/completion/retry/CI policies, 71 aliases/+1000 IDs, all receipts and real owners. No unrelated product change or global skill installation.
- The old source is held by a genuine independent Reviewer. That actual run must return it through supported ownership before the original Worker reclaims and edits. Record a fresh source handoff/review on the complete cumulative scope. Ordinary approval-only source, authorized frozen integration, independent combined review, all applicable checks, exact process-support and final-main proof remain required.
- This is a process-only update if and only if the exact immutable full diff plus independent product-isolation review proves it. No product-release request, unchanged Windows installer publication or application rollout is requested, and the earlier rejected product publication is not resumed. Mixed/unknown product effects must be investigated rather than waived.
- New pins install Pause support but do not activate outer8. Inspect real service/every-writer/adapter/CI/recovery readiness and actual live ownership. Only a compatible installed set and genuinely idle supported owned maintenance may perform pause activate preview/apply/resume. Do not stop/transfer foreign work merely to manufacture idleness, rewrite shared state or pretend old Todo-moving stops preserve phase. If genuine owners or unknown readiness block activation, retain the exact remaining boundary visibly pending rather than calling source merge live activation. No new scheduler or automatic restart.

### Additional acceptance for the cumulative update

- [ ] Exact published1.7.2/3.9.2 complete generated closure/provenance is adopted through the maintained upgrade; actual ACL local choices and current-main product inputs are preserved.
- [ ] ACL owner/operator guidance accurately describes the accumulated lifecycle, correction, activity and process-only delivery behavior, including genuine capacity/manual boundaries and conditional live Pause activation.

I rebuilt my resolved trial tree (main + my resolution) and compared it with 74eb343a. The `src` difference is limited to a removed comment, the order of the copy_more/file_vertical lines in app.py, and an en-dash in a JS comment. tests/test_acl1819_preflight.py adds the new 2-ad-set texts_dynamic parity fixtures.
