# Independent review: PR #974 / ACL-1358 (Issue #358). RETURNED (request-changes)

Reviewer-AS1025AB, session review_as1025ab_1358, lane b6f45b152bc2405c869231b1500226f8. Read-only worktree C:\acl-review-974 (detached at the head). No pushes, no live accounts, real token files not read.

- Head: 0fcfc9b43b5c157497e7dbc3af9418d9bd0f02bb. Base main 970a7a3c = the merge-base, so the head contains current main.
- Diff vs main: 16 files, all in ACL-1358 scope. The config/paths.py merge kept main's duplicate-key removal in `update_machine_env` (now inside the `.env` lock). Nothing from main was lost.

## What was checked against the previous review (Reviewer-A1021358)
1. Item 3 / Google scope: the owner split it out on 2026-10-25 (Issue comment). ACL-2175 = Issue #1175 exists (open, status:backlog) and also takes the ACL_UPDATE_TOKEN review. Accepted. Nit: the link only goes one way. #1175 says "Issue 358" as plain text, so GitHub has no cross-reference or sub-issue link, and #358 does not name #1175. Add "#1175" to the owner comment or the Issue, or make it a sub-issue.
2. No-leak tests: done and meaningful. Fake values have no token shape. They sit in the env, .env and both token files, plain and protected. The tests check the Sentry `_before_send`, the telemetry record, `to_row`, an old journal line, the upload error, the page capture folder (page.html and context.json), capture_to_fixture output and the support-bundle denylist. Masking is by value, only for values of 8 or more characters, and only for Multilogin JWTs and Google token, refresh, id and client secrets. I see no over-masking of normal report data. **But the per-call cost is a trap (B1).**
3. Packaged migration: `load_env()` runs `protect_machine_secrets()` first. It is idempotent (no extra backups), wrapped in try/except, and every per-file failure leaves the file as it was and becomes a note. A missing or locked file causes no crash and no crash loop. The `.env` lock waits at most 120 s and its timeout is caught. Tests run prepare_config_dir followed by load_env. OK.
4. Rollback: `acl_migrate_config.py --unprotect [--from-backup]` works for a source checkout (tests plus a real-DPAPI round trip in the windows_only file). It is documented in the fragment and in DELIVERY.md. **It is not usable on an installed app (B2).**
5. `protected-backup` is in SKIP_DIRS (tested). The windows_only marker is correct: test_token_vault_windows.py ran here and was not skipped. test_acl_test_platform is green.

## Blocking findings

**B1. Scrubbers decrypt or stat the token files on every call, which is a performance trap.**
`run_telemetry.scrub()`, `_hide_configured_secrets()`, `hide_secrets_deep()`, `capture_to_fixture.Scrubber.__call__` and `telemetry_sync.to_row` (once per cell) all call `token_vault.configured_secret_values()` again on every call. Each call goes through all of os.environ and runs `stat()` on each token file. The mtime cache only saves the decrypt. Measured on this Windows machine (Python 3.13) with two protected token files:
- `scrub()`: ~1.8 ms per call, against ~0.05 ms without the secret lookup (about 35x slower).
- `to_row()` over 2000 rows (the `upload` limit): **50 s**.
- `_before_send` on an event with 100 breadcrumbs: **1.9 s**, run synchronously in the thread that reports the error.
- `scrub_diag` runs scrub once per string, so every telemetry `record()` on the RPA path pays this cost several times.

Fix: compute the set once per top-level operation and pass it down. That means once per `scrub_diag` / `_before_send` event, once per `to_row` batch (or `pending()`), and once per capture or fixture. Alternatively, use a short time-based cache (a few seconds) around `configured_secret_values()` in addition to the mtime check. Add a test that bounds the number of stat/decrypt calls for a 2000-row batch and a 100-crumb event.

**B2. Rollback and downgrade do not work on installed (ACL.exe) machines, the very machines this round now migrates.**
- The documented command `python scripts/acl_migrate_config.py --unprotect` needs Python and a source checkout. The PyInstaller ACL.exe ships neither the script nor an interpreter (see packaging/windows/acl_windows.spec), and launcher.py has no matching switch. A buyer has no way to run the restore.
- The updater's automatic fallback (updater.py step 3: start the new version and wait for /health, otherwise start the previous one) runs from the OLD version. The new version's `serve.py` calls `load_env()` before `/health` answers, so the first update from a pre-1358 version protects the tokens even when the update then fails and rolls back. The old version then sends `dpapi:v1:...` as its Multilogin bearer token (401). Its `from_authorized_user_file` cannot parse the ACLDPAPI1 file, so it falls into the interactive InstalledAppFlow. DELIVERY.md admits this but points to the command that cannot be run there.

Fix, either or both:
- (a) Add a launcher switch, for example `ACL.exe --unprotect-tokens [--from-backup]`, that calls `paths.unprotect_machine_secrets()`. Document it in the fragment and DELIVERY.md, and cover it with a launcher test. The new version folder still exists after a fallback, so it can run there.
- (b) Do not protect on the packaged start until this version has proven healthy. For example, protect after `/health` first answers, or skip while an update is pending in `updates/` (`update_pending` / `last_update.json`).

At minimum, the changelog fragment (the buyer-facing release note) must state the consequence of a failed first update and the buyer's recovery: reconnect Multilogin and sign in to Google again, or run the switch from (a).

## Non-blocking notes
- N1. A shared machine folder with older instances: on the owner's machine every checkout or instance that uses the default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ACL` (for example 9090/main before 1358) will read ciphertext as soon as any 1358 build starts there. Before putting 1358 on TEST9095, either give it its own `ACL_CONFIG_DIR` or accept that 9090 needs Multilogin and Google reconnected. Say this in the handoff and changelog.
- N2. `--from-backup` and the "unreadable and nothing changed" branch of `unprotect_env_file` replace the whole `.env` with the pre-migration copy. Settings changed since then are lost, and a token reconnected since then reverts to the older one. Document this or merge only the token lines.
- N3. Backups are keyed by file name only. If `GSHEET_OAUTH_TOKEN` points outside the config dir, its backups mix with those of `<config>/token_accounts.json`.
- N4. `migrate_file` reads, seals and replaces without the lock that writers of the Google token use. A token refresh written by another process in that window can be overwritten by the older content. This is rare, and the refresh token usually survives.
- N5. DELIVERY.md should tell people to stop the dashboard before `--unprotect`, because the next `load_env()` in a running process (for example `ai_rescue`) protects the tokens again.

## Tests (Windows 11, Python 3.13, ACL_LIBRARY_*= empty, ACL_CONFIG_DIR = scratch)
These were run: test_acl1358_secrets_not_exported, test_acl1358_migration_and_rollback, test_token_vault, test_token_vault_windows (real DPAPI, not skipped), test_page_capture, test_capture_to_fixture, test_run_telemetry, test_machine_paths, test_google_machine_config, test_acl1558_scrubber_shapes, test_acl_test_platform, and packaging/windows/tests test_diagnostics, test_machine_config and test_launcher.

That is the B2 case again.

- **Cache invalidation.** The cache lives 5 s on a monotonic clock. Google values are also cached by mtime and size. `write_secret_text`, `protect_machine_secrets` and `unprotect_machine_secrets` reset it. The cache is a single tuple swap with no lock needed under the GIL.
- **Thread safety of the daemon.**

  - Writes are atomic, and the backup is written before the replace, so an exit mid-migration loses nothing.

## ACL-1768 review: PR #833 @ b44181ce (Reviewer-AS1025AU)

**Verdict: changes requested.** One blocking budget interaction, one red CI test, and the PR has to be merged with main 4c63ef0c. The rest (model, migration, per-ad-set fields, publish path, UI) is approvable once these are fixed.

### Blocking
1. **The create-call budget does not include the targeting reads (1768 x 1771).** `estimate_create_calls` counts writes, sets, ads and video polls. `_prepare` resolves targeting from the same client budget before any write, and the TermResolver job cap goes up to 90 reads. Reproduced with FakeMeta: 10 ad sets x 3 image ads, 3 work-position terms per set, cold SearchCache. Budget 240, resolver reads 71, all 30 ads written, then "Graph API stopped: call budget of 240 reached" during label/readback. So `success=false` comes after the writes. A slightly larger plan would stop part-way through creating. Fix: add a targeting reserve to the estimate, `min(JOB_READ_ABS_CAP, JOB_READ_BASE + JOB_READ_PER_TERM * distinct terms+parts across all ad sets)`. Or re-check after `_prepare` that the remaining budget is at least the write estimate, and refuse before the first write (same pattern as the ACL-1891 chunk check). Add a test with 2+ ad sets and non-exact terms.
2. **CI linux (3.13, 2) is red.** `tests/test_acl1891_video_chunks.py::test_the_default_budget_fits_a_typical_big_video_and_refuses_the_largest` fails with `assert (195 + 40) > 250`, because DEFAULT_CREATE_MAX_CALLS went from 150 to 250. It also fails locally at head. This is more than a constant: with a budget of 250, a plan of about 5 sets x 3 video ads lets a 1.5 GB video (195 chunk calls) pass the 1891 check, even though the other ads' writes also need that budget. Fix: count LargeFile chunk calls together with the plan estimate in the `_prepare` check (`chunk_calls + estimate > max_calls` → refuse up front). Then rewrite the 1891 test to check the effective per-plan budget instead of the constant.
   (tracker-link fails only because the task was not in Review; it is a process check.)

### Non-blocking (fix in the same refresh if cheap)
3. `resolve_pixel`: `facts.pixels and s.pixel_id not in facts.pixels`. When the account read returns no pixels, an ad set's own pixel is accepted unverified, and `elif all(s.pixel_id ...)` then returns. The campaign-level pixel is refused in the same situation. Drop the `facts.pixels and` guard.
4. Targeting per ad set stops at the first set. `_prepare` builds `[targeting_for(...) for s in plan.ad_sets]` and `interests()` raises `TargetingUnresolved` for set 1 before set 2 is prefetched. With N sets that need confirmation, Check plan reveals them one set per round. Prefetch and resolve the terms of all sets, then raise once with every item. The job cap already scales across sets: prefetch takes the max and counts `_results`, and this was checked with 2 and 10 sets.
5. Creative names use the campaign-wide ad number (`#{ad.index}`). Adding an ad to set 1 renumbers set 2. Ads are still reused by name per ad set, so nothing is duplicated. A creative left by a partial run under the old number is orphaned and a new one is created. Acceptable, but please note it in a comment or test.
6. Downgrade: an older page (VERSION 3) returns null for a v4 local or server draft, so drafts vanish if someone opens an older build against the same server draft store. Mention it in the changelog; no code change needed.

### Checked and OK
- Model and migration. Explicit `adset_index`; a slot without the key goes to set 0. Strict index parse with a refusal, never a guess. MAX_AD_SETS=10 on form, plan and page. The v3→v4 migration only adds missing keys (`in` guards), so it is idempotent, and v4 documents are untouched.
- No field loss. Golden check, same old single-ad-set form → slots (sorted) → drafts → preview → `plan_only` plan + audit: **byte-identical between main 4c63ef0c and the trial merge** (6135 bytes each).
- Per-ad-set fields: gender, languages, device, OS min, start time, pixel and language. Budget stays on the campaign (CBO) and is taken from the first slot.

src/web/app.py:2687-2697. `index` captures `_store_inputs` including selected CM before awaiting `_in_report_pool`. - P1 (cbPostPublish always called /connection/prepare, 409 rpa_backend broke RPA publishing): CLOSED. cbPostPublish prepares only when window.ACL_FB_BACKEND === 'api' (set from fb_backend at report.html:56); the RPA path goes straight to /publish-jobs exactly as before. aclPrepareConnection maps code rpa_backend to "nothing to prepare". Harness rpa-publish / rpa-409 cover it.
- Red CI: CLOSED, all checks green on ca55a607.
- API path keeps prepare + explicit reopen confirmation; same request_id retry skips prepare and reaches the server idempotency lookup (lost-publish mode). No Meta write replay found; the server-side prepare_existing only adopts/restarts under the reentrant physical lease and refuses an owned session ("busy").

Required fixes (new, API backend only):
1. [P1] A preparation refusal on Publish is reported as "Submission outcome unknown" and halts the whole batch. In cbPostPublish any rejection of aclPrepareConnection (declined reopen, 409 busy/profile_lease/stop_failed/restart_cooldown, non-JSON or lost /connection/prepare answer) is a plain Error, so post().catch -> halt(): the account is marked "Submission outcome unknown: ...", batch.uncertain=true and every other not-yet-sent account is settled "Not submitted: the status of another run in this tab is unknown". Nothing was sent in all these cases, so this contradicts spec item 5 ("say exactly which step failed; nothing is created") and stops unrelated accounts. Expected: a preparation refusal settles only that account as definitely not submitted with the stage message (e.g. "Not submitted: <reason>"); a lost/non-JSON prepare answer is either retryable (cbBusy -> offerRetry with the same request_id) or "not submitted", never "outcome unknown". Add harness modes: declined reopen, prepare 409 busy, prepare network failure -> no /publish-jobs call, no halt of the other accounts.
2. [P1] /connection/prepare takes the profile lease with timeout=0 (warm_api.prepare_connection: profile_lock(...).holding(timeout=0)). Before this PR a Publish for an account whose profile is momentarily held by a read (account refresh queue, Read spend, Check) or by its own running job queued behind it (PUBLISH_WAIT_SECONDS) or got the server's ACL-1603 duplicate answer (settled 'dup'). Now the client-side prepare fails immediately with code "connection" and, via item 1, halts the batch. Do not make Publish fail on a busy lease in pre-dispatch preparation: either skip client prepare when the profile is already warm/busy and let /publish-jobs queue/dedupe as before, or return a distinct code (busy) that the client treats as "submit anyway, the job will prepare itself" (ApiPublisher already calls prepare_existing inside the job under the blocking lease). Same timeout=0 now makes Read spend / Read countries on the API backend fail instead of waiting behind a running read - acceptable only if the message says so; prefer the same treatment.
3. [P3] On the API backend a dashboard not bound to 127.0.0.1 now refuses Read spend via prepare (_guard not_loopback) where the read itself previously ran. Confirm this is intended or skip prepare on not_loopback like rpa_backend.

Not blocking: harness covers the frontend paths; please add the regression cases from items 1-2 to tests/test_acl2092_connection_lifecycle.py.

# ACL-2258 independent review — PR 1259, head f80071d5, base main 46b70d04 (current main)

Verdict: changes requested.

Checked: creative_recovery.py, creator.py, targeting_resolver.py, changelog fragment; affected tests pass locally (112). Secrets: none.

## Blocking

1. `TermResolver._rejected_ids` falls back to ALL asked ids when Meta's "Invalid id" message names no id
   (`return named or set(asked)`). `_drop_cached_ids` then removes every matching term from the persistent
   ConfirmedStore, which holds human-confirmed picks. Reproduced: store with three confirmed interests
   (13-digit ids), `prefetch([...three terms...])`, fake Graph raising `GraphError("(#100) Invalid id")` for any
   `interest_fbid_list` -> no error is raised and the store is empty afterwards. One ambiguous Meta answer
   silently wipes all of the user's confirmations for the plan. The spec asks to drop "that cache entry" (the
   rejected id), not every cached one.
   Fix: drop only ids Meta names. When the message names none, either re-check the cached ids one at a time and
   drop only those Meta rejects individually, or raise as before (old behaviour). Add a test for the unnamed case
   that asserts the other confirmed entries survive.

## Non-blocking (fix while there)

2. `CampaignCreator._same_videos` docstring says each video "lies in this same account", and the GET asks for
   `account_id`, but the value is never compared. Either compare both `account_id` values to `plan.act` or fix
   the docstring; a safety claim that is not enforced on the publish path is misleading.
3. `video_pairs`: the list `patched` is built and never used (dead code).
4. Tests: add `_same_videos` cases for a GET error and for a missing `length` (both must return False — verified
   manually, they do), and for a different number of videos.
5. `_drop_cached_ids` removes the whole term (`store.remove(term)` drops every type, e.g. a confirmed
   behavior of the same term). Acceptable, but mention it in the comment.

## Verified as correct

- Receipt: foreign-account / non-schema / unparsable receipts still raise; only same act+identity with another
  fingerprint is treated as stale, and a stale receipt still goes through `candidates()` before any write.
- Video acceptance: only on `created`/`resumed_accepted` with a foreign tag; `matches()` on the patched params
  enforces account and all other content; GET error, missing or different length -> stop as before.
- Re-search recursion terminates: each retry strictly shrinks `ids`; with no ids an "Invalid id" error re-raises.
- Changelog fragment matches the change.

Affected tests in a detached worktree at a0ee3204 (tests/test_acl2231_creative_recovery.py, tests/test_acl1761_api_create.py, tests/test_acl1771_targeting_resolver.py): 243 passed. Branch contains main 46b70d04. No secrets in the diff.

## (a) Earlier fixes still intact

1. `_rejected_ids` drops only ids Meta named; an unnamed `Invalid id` still raises (unchanged since round 2; new comment explains the 10+ digit scrub, round-2 item B done).
2. Dead `patched` list stays removed.
3. Tests for GET error, missing length, other content and a different video count are present (their expected results changed where the owner relaxed the rule, see c).
4. Comment on `store.remove(term)` is present.
5. Receipt: same act+identity with another fingerprint is stale; foreign-account, non-schema and unparsable receipts still raise `creative_receipt`.

## (b) Live Graph request shape

`_same_videos` now asks `/{video_id}?fields=length` only. `length` is a field of the AdVideo node, so the round-2 `(#100) nonexisting field (account_id)` failure is gone. The fake `_Videos.get` rejects fields outside an AdVideo allow-list, and `test_video_reads_only_use_fields_that_exist_on_the_video_node` asserts the exact fields `["length", "length"]`. That assertion is what guards the request shape: since the relaxed rule swallows read errors, a bad field would no longer fail the length tests by itself.

## (c) Relaxed rules (owner decision, ACL-2250, ports of cd37d96a/5351b1ab)

Re-uploaded video id accepted even when unreadable:
- Reached only when Meta itself answered OUR write with this creative (`created`) or on resume of a receipt marked at that acceptance, with a foreign acl- tag and the same id, and `video_pairs` proves that after swapping in Meta's video ids every other requested field matches, account included (`matches` checks `account_id` of the creative). A creative found by name/listing never takes this path (candidates exclude foreign-tagged rows and use exact `matches`).
- So "different video content" is accepted only if Meta deduplicated our write onto a creative with another video AND neither length can be read. Meta's dedup answer is the main evidence. Another account cannot be accepted: the creative's account is checked and the video lives in that creative.
- Risk (bounded): if Meta's dedup were ever loose about videos and both video reads fail, the ad would use the earlier video. No new object is written by this path.
- Nit (non-blocking): the single `try` around the loop means the first unreadable video ends the check, so the lengths of later pairs (vertical file, ACL-1774) are not compared. A per-pair try/except would keep "stop only when both lengths are known and differ" true for every pair. The broad `except Exception` also accepts on token/rate-limit errors (read-only, so acceptable).

Several identical creatives -> oldest:
- Every candidate passed `complete` and the full `matches` (account, Page, form, all requested material) and is ours or untagged (foreign acl- tags excluded), so any of them satisfies the request; the oldest is deterministic. No write, no duplicate ad (ads are still found by exact name under our ad set). Safe.
- Residual: `matches` is a subset check, so two "identical" rows may differ in fields we never request (e.g. edited later in Ads Manager). That was already true for a single candidate.

Unknown-send receipt blocks 15 min (`RECEIPT_UNKNOWN_S = 900`):
- Age is the receipt file mtime, written by `receipt.save()` right before dispatch. The machine lock is held through the whole write, so a pending receipt seen later means the earlier process ended or the write raised; an HTTP request still in flight after 15 minutes is not realistic.
- After 15 minutes a new write happens only if a COMPLETE listing (all pages read, incomplete -> stop) shows no matching creative. The remaining double-send case is Meta having created the creative but not listing it after 15 minutes, or the earlier write carrying other media ids. Even then Meta answers an identical write with the existing creative (ACL-2249), and a real duplicate is a spare creative with no ad (no spend), which the oldest-rule then tolerates. Duplicate ads are not possible through this path.
- Receipts are machine-local: two machines on the same account were never protected by the receipt (unchanged).
- Nit (non-blocking): the module docstring of `creative_recovery.py` still says unknown dispatches "never expire into permission to create"; it should mention the 15-minute window in creator.py.

# ACL-2003 independent review - PR 1265, head c761e91c, base main 46b70d04 (current main; branch contains it)

Reviewer-R2003 (session rev_r2003_20261028). Verdict: approved, with non-blocking follow-ups below.

Scope: Issue 1003 items 1-4 and 6 per the owner amendment; item 5 (warm profile) deliberately absent. Files: src/web/publish_api.py, src/web/templates/report.html, tests, docs/system/PLAN_CHECK_TIMING.md, changelog fragment.

Tests in a fresh detached worktree at c761e91c: test_acl1761_plan_check, test_acl1819_failure_state, test_acl1819_preflight (runs the node gate harness), test_acl1990_partial_plan, test_acl2117_no_reopen_during_sync, test_acl1604_preflight, test_acl1771_targeting_resolver: 281 passed. Node harness tests/preflight_gate_harness.cjs (cases 9-12): ok. Browser tests not run. CI on the head: all checks pass (linux 1-3, windows, process, descriptor, tracker-link).

## Can a stale verdict hide a problem?
- Key: cbPfRev covers every field of the account form (account, country, link, etc.) plus the campaign's own camp_N_* fields, so budget/slot-set/account/country edits change the revision; a verdict is stored under the revision taken when the request started, so an edit during the check also invalidates it. Window 10 min (CB_PF_FRESH_MS); "Check again" always re-reads. Set widening is handled (cbPfStoredData returns null unless every slot is reusable).
- Account-state change inside 10 min (restricted account, payment, page) is not seen by the page, but Publish does not rely on it: the write path (/publish-jobs -> ApiPublisher._finish_open) runs preflight_account and plan building itself, independent of any saved verdict. The window is also stricter than before (previously a verdict was fresh by revision alone, with no time limit).
- A verdict that was an OK can only let the client gate pass; the gate is client-side and the server revalidates, so a stale OK cannot publish unvalidated.

## Server merge
- Key = (account casefold, country casefold, canonical JSON of the slots) so different drafts/budgets/accounts/countries never share. Leader failure of any kind (BaseException) is stored, the entry popped and the event set in finally, so waiters cannot hang; waiters get a deepcopy of the result or the same exception. Nothing is retained after the answer. Error text is the same text the leader's client would see (scrubbed by existing code).
- Not part of the key: confirm_reopen (see follow-up 3).

## Conflicts
git merge-tree of the head against PR 1261 and PR 1264 (and those two together) is clean; no textual conflicts in report.html or publish_api.py.

## Non-blocking follow-ups (not defects of this PR's goal)
1. Publish gate filters stale slots with cbPfFresh (revision + window) not cbPfReusable, so a "Could not check" (error_kind not_checked) younger than 10 min is not re-checked at Publish. Same as before the PR (it was revision-only), Publish is not blocked by design (ACL-1990) and the server revalidates, but it contradicts "a failed read never counts as a verdict". Suggest using cbPfReusable-equivalent in the gate.
2. Partial failure (error_kind plan/account with some campaigns unchecked) is stored per campaign and cbPfReusable treats it as reusable for 10 min; it is a blocking verdict, so it can only cause a false block, resolved by "Check again". Consider not reusing a hit that has an error and no result.
3. Server key ignores confirm_reopen: a request confirming reopening that joins a leader that got open_by_hand just gets that answer and re-prompts; the reverse merges an unconfirmed request into a confirmed leader. Harmless, worth a comment.
4. A single-flight subset caller (cbPreflightRun with fewer campaigns than the running one) receives the superset response; cbCheckPlan may then show extra campaigns. Cosmetic.

# ACL-2262 independent review - PR 1264, head 858294bd, base main 46b70d04 (current main)

Reviewer-R2262 (session rev_r2262_20261028). Verdict: changes requested.

The PR head contains current main 46b70d04, so no merge of main is needed. CI is red and the failures are real, not the known flaky ones.

## Blocking

1. CI fails because of this change. Linux shards 1 and 3 fail:
   - tests/test_acl1761_api_create.py::test_open_builds_a_read_only_client_and_page_for_a_dry_run[False|True]: "The profile could not be started with automation: MULTILOGIN_AUTOMATION_TOKEN_A is not set in .env"
   - tests/test_acl1761_hang_logout.py::test_open_stops_as_checkpoint, test_open_stops_as_logged_out_with_cooldown_and_no_graph_calls, test_page_unresponsive_cools_the_profile_for_ten_minutes: code is 'start_failed' instead of checkpoint/logged_out/page_unresponsive.
   Cause: `ApiPublisher.open` used to take the cold path (`_open_profile`) for a closed profile. Now `prepare_existing` sends every closed profile to `registry.open_one`, which calls the real MLX start. These tests cover the checkpoint, logged-out and frozen-tab stops on the publish open path. They have to keep passing, either through the warm path with fakes or by keeping the cold path where it applies. Do not just delete them. 2. Scope: account READS now open closed profiles and leave them open with no end. `prepare_existing` is shared. `account_spend_api._open_session` calls it for every read: spend reads, country split, turn-off commands, and `campaign_inventory` snapshot reads, which the automatic refresh queue runs in the 08/13/18 windows on 9090 and the installed build. Before this PR a closed, unregistered profile returned False on that path. The read then used the cold `_open_gated` path, which takes its own queue slot, and `_finish_started` closed the profile after the grace time, or it became a kept window with the ACL-2113 idle close or evictor. After this PR the same read opens the profile through `open_one` and registers it as a warm session. Warm sessions are closed only by "Close profiles" (`close_one`). There is no idle close, and the slot evictor does not reclaim them. One scheduled refresh would therefore open the profile of every dashboard account and keep all of them open. Memory fills up and later publishes fail with memory_low. It also means a timer, not a person, opens many live profiles at once and keeps them up.
   This breaks the owner rule (binding, delivered by the coordinator on 2026-10-28): a profile is brought up automatically NOT EARLIER THAN THE FIRST CAMPAIGN. A closed profile may be opened at Check plan and Publish, and for actions the user starts on an account. It must never be opened on page load, from background, scheduled or stat reads, or just because an account was added to the Builder.
   Where each caller stands at 858294bd:
   - src/web/publish_api.py ApiPublisher._open_warm: Check plan (dry run) and Publish. OPENS a closed profile. Allowed.
   - src/web/warm_api.py prepare_connection (/connection/prepare): called only from report.html cbPostPublish, which runs before Publish. OPENS a closed profile. Allowed.
   - src/analysis_agent/account_spend_api.py _open_session, line ~580: every account read (spend, country split, campaign_inventory snapshot, automatic refresh queue, turn-off commands). OPENS a closed profile without any campaign. BLOCKER.
   Nothing calls it on page load. aclConnectionFetch has no callers.
   Requested fix (adopt-only on reads): make auto-open an explicit choice of the caller. For example, a ContextVar or a parameter like `confirmed_reopen`, set by `ApiPublisher.open` (Check plan and Publish) and by `/connection/prepare`. Reads keep the old result (False, then the cold path with its close or kept-window rules). The "registered but process gone" and "port changed" re-adoption can stay for all callers, because it only fixes stale registry records. Add a test that a read of a closed, unregistered profile does not call `open_one`.

3. `release_frozen_tab_cooldown` turns the 10-minute frozen-tab wait off completely under managed sessions. It runs at the start of every read and every publish open. If the replacement tab also hangs, `_start_cooldown` arms the wait again, and the next action, including the next scheduled read or the next account in a batch, drops it again. A browser that is really frozen then gets a new tab and a full READY_TIMEOUT wait on every action. That is hammering of a hung profile. It also runs before we know whether the warm path will be used: `prepare_existing` can still return False (closing, unknown, no_port without permission, restart wait) and the cold path then opens a tab with no wait.
   Requested fix: allow one replacement per frozen episode. Mark the cooldown as "released once". If the replacement also stops as page_unresponsive, keep the full wait. Release only when the action will go through the warm checkout. Add a test: frozen, then replaced, then frozen again keeps the wait for the next action.

4. Add account: the task text asks to open the profile when an account is added to the Builder. The owner rule above overrides that (not earlier than the first campaign). 5. `HAND_MESSAGE` ("... wait about 3 minutes, then use Open profiles for today") and the OPEN chip title ("Use Open profiles for today to keep it ready") still point to the button and the 3 minutes. The spec says nothing may depend on the button.
6. In the new kind == "none" plus registered branch, `_forget(pid, stopped=True)` records the stop at the moment it is found, not when the profile really closed (possibly hours ago). The code default of ACL_PROFILE_RESTART_COOLDOWN_S is still 180 s; 0 is only in the owner's machine .env. On any machine without that setting, `open_one` refuses with "about 3 min" right after it detects the closed profile. Consider stopped=False here, or say in the text that the wait is only for machines with a cooldown.

- Race (profile closed right after the check): checkout's `_verify_process` raises profile_closed with a clear text. No retry storm.

`_same_videos` now asks `/{video_id}?fields=length` only. `length` is a field of the AdVideo node, so the round-2 `(#100) nonexisting field (account_id)` failure is gone. The fake `_Videos.get` rejects fields outside an AdVideo allow-list, and `test_video_reads_only_use_fields_that_exist_on_the_video_node` asserts the exact fields `["length", "length"]`. That assertion is what guards the request shape: since the relaxed rule swallows read errors, a bad field would no longer fail the length tests by itself.

## (c) Relaxed rules (owner decision, ACL-2250, ports of cd37d96a/5351b1ab)

Re-uploaded video id accepted even when unreadable:
- Reached only when Meta itself answered OUR write with this creative (`created`) or on resume of a receipt marked at that acceptance, with a foreign acl- tag and the same id, and `video_pairs` proves that after swapping in Meta's video ids every other requested field matches, account included (`matches` checks `account_id` of the creative). A creative found by name/listing never takes this path (candidates exclude foreign-tagged rows and use exact `matches`).
- So "different video content" is accepted only if Meta deduplicated our write onto a creative with another video AND neither length can be read. Meta's dedup answer is the main evidence. Another account cannot be accepted: the creative's account is checked and the video lives in that creative.
- Risk (bounded): if Meta's dedup were ever loose about videos and both video reads fail, the ad would use the earlier video. No new object is written by this path.
- Nit (non-blocking): the single `try` around the loop means the first unreadable video ends the check, so the lengths of later pairs (vertical file, ACL-1774) are not compared. A per-pair try/except would keep "stop only when both lengths are known and differ" true for every pair. The broad `except Exception` also accepts on token/rate-limit errors (read-only, so acceptable).

Several identical creatives -> oldest:
- Every candidate passed `complete` and the full `matches` (account, Page, form, all requested material) and is ours or untagged (foreign acl- tags excluded), so any of them satisfies the request; the oldest is deterministic. No write, no duplicate ad (ads are still found by exact name under our ad set). Safe.
- Residual: `matches` is a subset check, so two "identical" rows may differ in fields we never request (e.g. edited later in Ads Manager). That was already true for a single candidate.

Unknown-send receipt blocks 15 min (`RECEIPT_UNKNOWN_S = 900`):
- Age is the receipt file mtime, written by `receipt.save()` right before dispatch. The machine lock is held through the whole write, so a pending receipt seen later means the earlier process ended or the write raised; an HTTP request still in flight after 15 minutes is not realistic.
- After 15 minutes a new write happens only if a COMPLETE listing (all pages read, incomplete -> stop) shows no matching creative. The remaining double-send case is Meta having created the creative but not listing it after 15 minutes, or the earlier write carrying other media ids. Even then Meta answers an identical write with the existing creative (ACL-2249), and a real duplicate is a spare creative with no ad (no spend), which the oldest-rule then tolerates. Duplicate ads are not possible through this path.
- Receipts are machine-local: two machines on the same account were never protected by the receipt (unchanged).
- Nit (non-blocking): the module docstring of `creative_recovery.py` still says unknown dispatches "never expire into permission to create"; it should mention the 15-minute window in creator.py.

  Content-Length over the route limit → 413 without calling the app; invalid/negative
  Content-Length → 400; chunked/understated bodies counted per message and cut at the
  first byte over the limit; an app that swallows the overflow still answers 413;

1026.title: Update ACL shared workflow and task lifecycle support
1026.body:
## Description
Adopt the shared Task Tracker and Master Repo support that distinguishes a task's workflow category from an executor's confirmed activity. ACL should show honest work time and explain movement into and out of Review using the common implementation, so an occupied slot or an old Review label cannot look like continuous work.

## Specifications
### Context and expected behavior
- Owner authorized the common fix and ACL adoption on 2026-10-19. The shared implementation belongs to [TT-174](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/174); shared rules and exact export/pin support belong to [MR-65](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/65).
- Current ACL selects Master 1.5.3 `6f7e9416e68c66484a3b6c0213eab24847005b8f` and Tracker 3.7.1 `be87599d1b5e625058bbddc33c35bda86687b5bf`. Implementation waits for accepted exact compatible upstream revisions.
- Workflow status, recorded ownership and confirmed executor activity remain separate. An old or silent executor is unknown, never automatically stopped or released. Work time must not grow through unconfirmed activity or waiting intervals. Existing Review history must remain available through the common Tracker projection.

### Scope and constraints
- Update compatible exact standard/engine pins and the maintained exported helpers/generated selected guide using the native upgrade procedure, plus truthful ACL instructions and the guarded operator adapter only if necessary for shared client integration.
- Use the shared executor activity contract. Do not create ACL-specific heartbeat/presence logic or a detached process that confirms an idle executor.
- Preserve descriptor2, package profile and target, draft adoption, active execution3 with 5/5/5 limits, process1, Stage disabled with permanent stage retained, absent optional context/completion/retry/native-CI policies, all required checks, 71 historical aliases and +1000 task numbering, historical receipts and genuine ownership.
- No campaign runtime changes, live advertising actions, state migration, clearing another owner's claim, or package run without the real supported admission/delivery route.
- Fulfilled upstream prerequisite: [TT-174](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/174), native Merged; published Tracker [v3.7.3](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/releases/tag/v3.7.3) at `5d0a915c9fdb8dea4e3aded38beaa8dd1a024ecc`, verified 2026-10-20.
- Fulfilled upstream prerequisite: [MR-65](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/65), closed/Merged; published Master [v1.5.4](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/releases/tag/v1.5.4) at `10da6de5b496a21e10188f2df63bef1f0254afbf`, verified 2026-10-20.
- Original planning prerequisite: actual reviewed revisions had to be verified before implementation; external references were unresolved until inspection. Both are now verified above. The shared reader/service is published; ACL consumer adoption remains this task.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ACL pins accepted compatible shared revisions and generated/portable artifacts match their actual upstream manifests.
- [ ] ACL's guarded adapter reaches shared activity operations without bypassing adoption checks; any required integration change has focused behavioral coverage.
- [ ] Selected guide and local instructions describe confirmed activity, waiting and unknown activity truthfully, preserving workflow categories and existing ownership/review/delivery controls.
- [ ] Existing ACL policy choices, IDs, historical evidence and unrelated product/runtime files remain unchanged.
- [ ] Separate non-implementing source review, applicable checks and genuine existing frozen-batch admission/delivery are completed or their concrete remaining blocker is recorded accurately.
- [ ] Actual source adoption and reader/writer/publication verification are recorded separately; source pins alone are never reported as live activation.

### Implementation and verification
- Route is the existing ordinary approval-only source PR into main, independent source review, Approved, authorized Coordinator's frozen batch with independent combined review, required exact checks and the genuine package completion condition. Policy/config/helper edits cannot use the instruction-only shortcut.
- Worker: Worker-ACT174A, an actual isolated agent session. Coordinator: Coordinator-ACT174, actual session recorded privately. Acquire a real implementation claim only when upstream dependencies and actual repository capacity permit implementation.
- Check exact export/descriptor consistency and focused ACL adapter/adoption regression tests first; preserve required hosted Linux/Windows/installer checks. Review existing unchanged evidence before requesting more checks.

### Handoff
- 2026-10-19: planned dependent adoption; no implementation claim, PR, code edit, migration or delivery yet. Exact upstream accepted pins are pending from the owning Coordinator. Duplicate search found no current task owning this shared executor activity adoption; older tracking/adoption tasks retain their original scope.

- 2026-10-20: fulfilled upstream prerequisites verified at the exact published pair above. Original requirements, acceptance criteria and historical planning remain preserved. No implementation claim yet at this checkpoint.

### Latest owner amendment — global process/product separation — 2026-10-20
- The owner explicitly required process updates to be delivered separately from the product for every repository and installation profile, then instructed implementation. This task continues the original activity-support adoption and now adopts that global process-only completion boundary as part of the same shared-support upgrade.
- For this proven isolated process outcome, the latest instruction supersedes the earlier plan's assumption that an ACL Windows installer publication is necessary merely because ACL uses the package profile. The original plan and criteria above remain historical evidence. Actual product/runtime/installation changes and explicit product-publication requests retain their original package checks and delivery; this task requests none of them.
- Published support verified: Master [v1.6.0](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/releases/tag/v1.6.0) at `6cbc2bbfd5df76fc2f1ad6f285d33a45dd5ff504`, compatible Tracker [v3.8.0](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/releases/tag/v3.8.0) at `9c3ad4deec6b3596d5ef48400430b126155012dd`. Shared work: [TT-177](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/177) and [MR-68](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/68). These publication prerequisites are verified independently of each Issue's broader lifecycle; no active external dependency marker is being inferred as a local task.
- The genuine Coordinator returned the old Approved source for author revision using the maintained command before this amendment. Prior `ca9a650` source approval and all original history remain preserved; they do not approve this changed scope or future head. Keep original PR1027, author, branch and isolated worktree. All unrelated owners and five source-review reservations remain untouched.
- Preserve all non-pin descriptor fields exactly as actual main, including its historical explanatory exception; put current support explanations in repository prose. Tracker config, layout, product/build/install/update/release inputs, all policies/targets/checks, IDs and prior receipts remain unchanged. Inspect actual imports and indirect build inputs, not directory names alone.
- Obtain read-only canonical process-support proof from the published pair for the complete immutable candidate diff. A genuine independent Reviewer must assess the entire amended task and add exact-scope `process_support` evidence, including actual product isolation. Preserve ordinary source approval, frozen-batch composition, independent combined review and all applicable checks/main admission; this is not the schema1 instruction-only shortcut.
- No consumer product delivery request, Windows publication, migration or foreign-owner recovery is authorized or created here. The earlier automatically rejected Windows publication is not resumed. Process completion requires the supported exact admitted-main proof; unknown or mixed content stays unfinished.

### Additional acceptance for the owner amendment
- [ ] The final candidate uses the exact published canonical pair and passes native read-only process-support preflight; scope-bound independent review verifies the full process-only outcome and real product isolation.
- [ ] Ordinary source/batch/combined/main review and required checks remain enforced, with supported process delivery and completion evidence after actual main integration.
- [ ] No consumer installer, application deployment, product-release request or reinterpretation of an existing product receipt is used to complete this isolated process task.


### Latest owner amendment — one cumulative ACL update — 2026-10-20

ACL-1784 / PR #961 independent source review — RETURNED for a fix (Reviewer-A1021784, head a525a67a, contains main ea41acbf).

Scope checked: full diff vs work/main (CHANGELOG, src/web/publish_api.py, src/web/publish_jobs.py, new tests/test_acl1784_api_review_window.py), the Issue spec/acceptance, PR body (one `Tracker issues: ACL-1784` line, no closing keywords), merge commit a525a67a (`git show --cc`: only CHANGELOG adjacent entries, resolved correctly, no code touched). No leaked ids/tokens/paths; notices are English; RPA path unchanged (`review_window` never set there). Local tests: test_acl1784_api_review_window, test_acl1603_stable_slots, test_acl1761_*, test_acl1614_cancel_hung_job, test_acl1812_warm_sessions — 404 passed.

BLOCKING finding B1 — the slot is released while a profile the job started is still running, and the panel says the opposite.

In `_run_api`, `settled = clean or not wrote` drives both `review_window = not settled` (which makes `_run_job_inner` call `_slots.release` instead of `_slots.keep`) and the notice. But `ApiPublisher.finish_job` can still return "" (profile left open) for a job-started profile even when `clean=True`:
- `self.cancelled()` — user pressed Stop before the first write (cancel_job intentionally leaves the Multilogin window open, ACL-1614);
- `_keep_profiles_open()` — owner switch ACL_KEEP_PROFILES_OPEN;
- `self.dry_run` — finish_job forces clean=False (dry_run=1 jobs are reachable from the publish endpoint);
- `_stop_profile` raised (stop failure).
In all of these, wrote=False → settled=True → review_window=False → the slot is freed, yet the Mimic window the job started keeps running. That is exactly the hazard ACL-1603 guards against (queue launching extra Mimics over open windows; with cap 1 a second profile starts while the first is still open). The panel then shows API_NO_WRITE_NOTICE "the profile is not kept open for review", which is false. The Stop-before-first-write case also misses the Issue spec ("stops before the first write" → close our tab, release the slot, stop the profile if the job started it): the profile is neither stopped nor counted.

Required fix (either is acceptable, keep it small):
(a) Release the slot only when the profile is actually not left open by the job: `outcome == "closed"` OR the job did not start the profile (user-opened — spec says release in that case). If a job-started profile stays open for any other reason (cancel, keep-open switch, dry run, stop failure), keep the slot as before and do not show the "not kept open" notice (show an accurate one or none). And/or
(b) For a no-write stop, let finish_job stop the job-started profile despite `cancelled()` (spec), and still fall back to (a) when stopping did not happen.
Expose what you need from ApiPublisher read-only (e.g. a `started_profile` property from `self._opened.started_now`) rather than reaching into privates.

Tests to add (fakes; the current FakePublisher.finish_job does not model cancel/keep-open/dry-run/stop-failure, so it cannot catch this): Stop before the first write on a job-started profile; ACL_KEEP_PROFILES_OPEN=1 with a clean no-write or clean job on a job-started profile; finish_job returning "" for a job-started profile — each must either close the profile or keep the slot, and the notice must match the real state. Prefer driving the real `ApiPublisher.finish_job` with a faked `_opened`/`_stop_profile` for at least one case.

Non-blocking notes:
- `wrote` falls back to True on an exception — good (conservative).
- GraphError rejections count as writes (`GraphClient.writes` increments before POST), so a Meta-refused write keeps the window — conservative, acceptable.
- CI on a525a67a: all test/installer/descriptor checks green; `tracker-link` failed because it ran before handoff ("move it to Review before a ready PR") — rerun it on the next head.

1079.title: Adopt isolated manual verification completion support
1079.body:
## Description

Adopt the reviewed shared support that lets an actually verified, isolated manual process task finish without publishing an unchanged ACL installer. Preserve ACL application behavior, its local workflow safeguards and all other developers' ownership/history. Then validate that the adopted native client supports the real ACL-2071 completion; recording its separate supplemental receipt remains tied to the original task and genuine independent assessment.

## Specifications

Owner authorization: complete the process-completion fix end to end, with a compatible shared release and separately reviewed ACL adoption. Use existing schema3 capacity and preserve incumbent claims; no ownership exception or migration is requested. Current published selections are Master1.7.2 at4f148cbbbc2c9c65a7fdebba9b37551f91566e04 and Tracker3.9.2 at3d32586d72e4621f70d56d35f1e199a19fa13b00. Targets are independently reviewed, genuinely published Master1.8.0 at fddcdd0d60db2e14cce0a53e6af23e12356c3bc7 (v1.8.0, release420144866) and Tracker3.10.0 at e71c9829247e60d79031dbb1bb038896fcedf4cc (v3.10.0, release420140493). Actual-main checks and clean immutable no-override portable3.9 pair39691739580 passed.

Related work: TT194/PR195 and MR77 provide the compatible support. ACL2069/PR1070 belongs to the original developer with its own reserved3.9.4/1.7.3 scope; preserve that source, owner and original acceptance. This task adopts the distinct isolated_verification1 capability and does not silently complete or supersede2069.

Scope: use the maintained three-way standard upgrade against actual published official sources; inspect every local conflict. Only canonical separated process support, precise standard/engine pins, generated selected navigation/templates and relevant repository process knowledge may change. Preserve ACL's guarded scripts/acl_task_tracker.py, .workflow/adoption.json, project-specific instructions, schema3 execution with five workers/five source reviewers/batch5, disabled Stage choice, delivery target/checks/authorization, native status/ID/history policies and all state/ownership. Do not activate optional completion/context/retry/pause policies, seize foreign slots, rewrite frozen tasks, add a controller or publish an unchanged product.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Exact stable Master/Tracker releases, immutable commits and complete trusted export closure are verified; maintained upgrade preserves all local controls and non-pin selections.
- [ ] Whole product/source/configuration/build/install/update/publication scope is independently assessed; unchanged product installer is not requested for a genuinely canonical process-only support batch. Existing genuine product publication requests remain unchanged.
- [ ] Required source/main/process/descriptor and relevant shared delivery-tool regressions pass on the exact candidate; current independent source and combined reviews bind complete original scope/proof.
- [ ] Normal old-pin source approval and frozen integration admission are used under real ownership, when the integration slot is available. Actual main includes the complete reviewed scope without a product delivery request; the existing native completion procedure remains required.
- [ ] Fresh guarded client and deployed compatible reader validate adopted selections, unchanged incumbent owners/policies/history, and supported ACL2071 preview. Actual ACL2071 supplemental completion is verified separately against its original acceptance and official successful Windows run.

Checks: project descriptor and tracker-link/process admission, affected canonical support/upgrade/guard/delivery-governance regressions, exact immutable diff inspection and actual native/public readback. Full required CI is not waived. Product/runtime verification is required only if actual changes or indirect consumption invalidate the reviewed process-only proof.

Handoff: owner-selected support adoption, not started by Issue creation alone. Actual current main64e73a1e and old pins were reread. Read-only maintained upgrade stopped at two genuine local text conflicts in delivery-check.yml and VERIFICATION.md without writing; resolve explicitly preserving ACL master push/draft validation and stronger verification guidance. Shared service deployment awaits a separate concrete security approval; prepare only under the currently adopted old client. No new isolated receipt writer may activate ahead of the deployed reader. Source owner must verify actual available capacity and real In Progress before edits.

- **Remaining-budget comment is inaccurate.** The comments say "if writes don't fit after the reads, `_prepare` refuses before the first write". One edge: the resolver is shared across campaigns of one job, and its job cap is cumulative (`len(_results)`), so a later campaign can in theory read more than its own reserve. Cheap hardening for a follow-up: an unconditional `client.max_calls - client.calls < estimate_create_calls(plan)` refusal at the end of `_prepare` when writing.
- **The concurrent-confirm test failure is not a lock race.** The 1771 test `test_concurrent_confirms_do_not_lose_entries` (11 == 12 under load) passes in my full group run and in 150 extra 12-thread loops. `ConfirmedStore.put` holds `_STORE_LOCK` around read → modify → atomic replace, so in-process writes are serialized. The likely cause is a transient Windows file-sharing error (AV/indexer) on `os.replace` or `_read`.
  - It does expose a real 1771 robustness gap, so I suggest a follow-up task for 1771 (not this PR):
    - `_read` maps any OSError, including PermissionError, to `{}`, and the next `put` would then rewrite the file with only the new entry, dropping the confirmed cache;

  - Fix: on a read error other than file-not-found, refuse to write or retry, and retry the replace on PermissionError.

1026.title: Update ACL shared workflow and task lifecycle support
1026.body:
## Description
Adopt the shared Task Tracker and Master Repo support that distinguishes a task's workflow category from an executor's confirmed activity. ACL should show honest work time and explain movement into and out of Review using the common implementation, so an occupied slot or an old Review label cannot look like continuous work.

## Specifications
### Context and expected behavior
- Owner authorized the common fix and ACL adoption on 2026-10-19. The shared implementation belongs to [TT-174](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/174); shared rules and exact export/pin support belong to [MR-65](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/65).
- Current ACL selects Master 1.5.3 `6f7e9416e68c66484a3b6c0213eab24847005b8f` and Tracker 3.7.1 `be87599d1b5e625058bbddc33c35bda86687b5bf`. Implementation waits for accepted exact compatible upstream revisions.
- Workflow status, recorded ownership and confirmed executor activity remain separate. An old or silent executor is unknown, never automatically stopped or released. Work time must not grow through unconfirmed activity or waiting intervals. Existing Review history must remain available through the common Tracker projection.

### Scope and constraints
- Update compatible exact standard/engine pins and the maintained exported helpers/generated selected guide using the native upgrade procedure, plus truthful ACL instructions and the guarded operator adapter only if necessary for shared client integration.
- Use the shared executor activity contract. Do not create ACL-specific heartbeat/presence logic or a detached process that confirms an idle executor.
- Preserve descriptor2, package profile and target, draft adoption, active execution3 with 5/5/5 limits, process1, Stage disabled with permanent stage retained, absent optional context/completion/retry/native-CI policies, all required checks, 71 historical aliases and +1000 task numbering, historical receipts and genuine ownership.
- No campaign runtime changes, live advertising actions, state migration, clearing another owner's claim, or package run without the real supported admission/delivery route.
- Fulfilled upstream prerequisite: [TT-174](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/174), native Merged; published Tracker [v3.7.3](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/releases/tag/v3.7.3) at `5d0a915c9fdb8dea4e3aded38beaa8dd1a024ecc`, verified 2026-10-20.
- Fulfilled upstream prerequisite: [MR-65](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/65), closed/Merged; published Master [v1.5.4](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/releases/tag/v1.5.4) at `10da6de5b496a21e10188f2df63bef1f0254afbf`, verified 2026-10-20.
- Original planning prerequisite: actual reviewed revisions had to be verified before implementation; external references were unresolved until inspection. Both are now verified above. The shared reader/service is published; ACL consumer adoption remains this task.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ACL pins accepted compatible shared revisions and generated/portable artifacts match their actual upstream manifests.
- [ ] ACL's guarded adapter reaches shared activity operations without bypassing adoption checks; any required integration change has focused behavioral coverage.
- [ ] Selected guide and local instructions describe confirmed activity, waiting and unknown activity truthfully, preserving workflow categories and existing ownership/review/delivery controls.
- [ ] Existing ACL policy choices, IDs, historical evidence and unrelated product/runtime files remain unchanged.
- [ ] Separate non-implementing source review, applicable checks and genuine existing frozen-batch admission/delivery are completed or their concrete remaining blocker is recorded accurately.
- [ ] Actual source adoption and reader/writer/publication verification are recorded separately; source pins alone are never reported as live activation.

### Implementation and verification
- Route is the existing ordinary approval-only source PR into main, independent source review, Approved, authorized Coordinator's frozen batch with independent combined review, required exact checks and the genuine package completion condition. Policy/config/helper edits cannot use the instruction-only shortcut.
- Worker: Worker-ACT174A, an actual isolated agent session. Coordinator: Coordinator-ACT174, actual session recorded privately. Acquire a real implementation claim only when upstream dependencies and actual repository capacity permit implementation.
- Check exact export/descriptor consistency and focused ACL adapter/adoption regression tests first; preserve required hosted Linux/Windows/installer checks. Review existing unchanged evidence before requesting more checks.

### Handoff
- 2026-10-19: planned dependent adoption; no implementation claim, PR, code edit, migration or delivery yet. Exact upstream accepted pins are pending from the owning Coordinator. Duplicate search found no current task owning this shared executor activity adoption; older tracking/adoption tasks retain their original scope.

- 2026-10-20: fulfilled upstream prerequisites verified at the exact published pair above. Original requirements, acceptance criteria and historical planning remain preserved. No implementation claim yet at this checkpoint.

### Latest owner amendment — global process/product separation — 2026-10-20
- The owner explicitly required process updates to be delivered separately from the product for every repository and installation profile, then instructed implementation. This task continues the original activity-support adoption and now adopts that global process-only completion boundary as part of the same shared-support upgrade.
- For this proven isolated process outcome, the latest instruction supersedes the earlier plan's assumption that an ACL Windows installer publication is necessary merely because ACL uses the package profile. The original plan and criteria above remain historical evidence. Actual product/runtime/installation changes and explicit product-publication requests retain their original package checks and delivery; this task requests none of them.
- Published support verified: Master [v1.6.0](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/releases/tag/v1.6.0) at `6cbc2bbfd5df76fc2f1ad6f285d33a45dd5ff504`, compatible Tracker [v3.8.0](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/releases/tag/v3.8.0) at `9c3ad4deec6b3596d5ef48400430b126155012dd`. Shared work: [TT-177](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/177) and [MR-68](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/68). These publication prerequisites are verified independently of each Issue's broader lifecycle; no active external dependency marker is being inferred as a local task.
- The genuine Coordinator returned the old Approved source for author revision using the maintained command before this amendment. Prior `ca9a650` source approval and all original history remain preserved; they do not approve this changed scope or future head. Keep original PR1027, author, branch and isolated worktree. All unrelated owners and five source-review reservations remain untouched.
- Preserve all non-pin descriptor fields exactly as actual main, including its historical explanatory exception; put current support explanations in repository prose. Tracker config, layout, product/build/install/update/release inputs, all policies/targets/checks, IDs and prior receipts remain unchanged. Inspect actual imports and indirect build inputs, not directory names alone.
- Obtain read-only canonical process-support proof from the published pair for the complete immutable candidate diff. A genuine independent Reviewer must assess the entire amended task and add exact-scope `process_support` evidence, including actual product isolation. Preserve ordinary source approval, frozen-batch composition, independent combined review and all applicable checks/main admission; this is not the schema1 instruction-only shortcut.
- No consumer product delivery request, Windows publication, migration or foreign-owner recovery is authorized or created here. The earlier automatically rejected Windows publication is not resumed. Process completion requires the supported exact admitted-main proof; unknown or mixed content stays unfinished.

### Additional acceptance for the owner amendment
- [ ] The final candidate uses the exact published canonical pair and passes native read-only process-support preflight; scope-bound independent review verifies the full process-only outcome and real product isolation.
- [ ] Ordinary source/batch/combined/main review and required checks remain enforced, with supported process delivery and completion evidence after actual main integration.
- [ ] No consumer installer, application deployment, product-release request or reinterpretation of an existing product receipt is used to complete this isolated process task.


### Latest owner amendment — one cumulative ACL update — 2026-10-20

The owner explicitly instructed proceeding with one ACL update task after reviewing the completed shared releases. This replaces the earlier defer-ACL restriction for this task. Reuse ACL-2026 / source PR1027 and preserve the complete original requirements, decisions, reviews and handoffs; no duplicate adoption task is needed.

The shared snapshot service is already deployed at3d32586d72e4621f70d56d35f1e199a19fa13b00. These facts are prerequisites, not ACL adoption proof.
- Include the accumulated common process changes: truthful owner-confirmed activity and native task history; process/product delivery separation; phase-preserving explicit Pause/Resume support; approved waiting work in Delivery as Ready for integration; genuine Needs fixes in Backlog and actually owned Fixing in In Progress; fresh independent Review after corrections; continuation of the already owner-selected task set under actual capacity/admission, with existing explicit pause/new-work/integration decisions. Retain five categories and configured native keys. The shared header cleanup is already delivered by the shared reader.
- Current actual ACLmain is259ae7f (full SHA recorded with final source evidence). Assess its unrelated completed product changes; preserve them in the candidate. Use the maintained three-way upgrade and genuine pristine baseline, reconciling local instruction overlaps intentionally. Preserve descriptor2, all non-pin descriptor fields, config/layout/policies, package target/checks, 5/5/5 capacities, no Stage with permanent stage history, absent optional context/completion/retry/CI policies, 71 aliases/+1000 IDs, all receipts and real owners. No unrelated product change or global skill installation.
- The old source is held by a genuine independent Reviewer. That actual run must return it through supported ownership before the original Worker reclaims and edits. Record a fresh source handoff/review on the complete cumulative scope. Ordinary approval-only source, authorized frozen integration, independent combined review, all applicable checks, exact process-support and final-main proof remain required.
- This is a process-only update if and only if the exact immutable full diff plus independent product-isolation review proves it. No product-release request, unchanged Windows installer publication or application rollout is requested, and the earlier rejected product publication is not resumed. Mixed/unknown product effects must be investigated rather than waived.
- New pins install Pause support but do not activate outer8. Inspect real service/every-writer/adapter/CI/recovery readiness and actual live ownership. Only a compatible installed set and genuinely idle supported owned maintenance may perform pause activate preview/apply/resume. Do not stop/transfer foreign work merely to manufacture idleness, rewrite shared state or pretend old Todo-moving stops preserve phase. If genuine owners or unknown readiness block activation, retain the exact remaining boundary visibly pending rather than calling source merge live activation. No new scheduler or automatic restart.

### Additional acceptance for the cumulative update

- [ ] Exact published1.7.2/3.9.2 complete generated closure/provenance is adopted through the maintained upgrade; actual ACL local choices and current-main product inputs are preserved.
- [ ] ACL owner/operator guidance accurately describes the accumulated lifecycle, correction, activity and process-only delivery behavior, including genuine capacity/manual boundaries and conditional live Pause activation.

No leaked ids/tokens/paths (account labels only, as in the Issue). User-facing notices English. RPA path unchanged (review_window never set there).
Acceptance: plan error leaves no kept window and the next queued job starts at cap 1; preflight stop closes a job-started profile and frees the slot for a user-opened one; clean job releases its slot (closes a job-started profile); readback mismatch / error after a write keeps the window. Tests use fake publisher and real ProfileSlots; the real finish_job is exercised for clean/stop/keep-open/dry-run/stop-failure.
Earlier blocking finding B1 (slot freed while a job-started profile stayed open, false notice) is fixed: still_open = outcome != 'closed' and started_profile keeps the slot and shows API_STILL_OPEN_NOTICE.
Non-blocking: on a user Stop before the first write the job-started profile is not stopped (ACL-1614 leaves the window open on cancel); the slot stays taken and the notice is truthful. I accept this as a conservative reading of the Issue's 'stops before the first write', which plan/preflight stops satisfy; owner may ask for auto-stop later. Writes counter counts Meta-refused POSTs as writes (conservative). The fix was written before the worker claim and committed after it (process note only).
Tests run locally: test_acl1784, test_acl1603, test_acl1761_api_create, test_acl1761_plan_check, test_acl1614, test_a_finished_clean_profile_closes_itself, test_acl1812: 365 passed.

lane.report:
ACL-1784 / PR #961 independent source review — RETURNED for a fix (Reviewer-A1021784, head a525a67a, contains main ea41acbf).

Scope checked: full diff vs work/main (CHANGELOG, src/web/publish_api.py, src/web/publish_jobs.py, new tests/test_acl1784_api_review_window.py), the Issue spec/acceptance, PR body (one `Tracker issues: ACL-1784` line, no closing keywords), merge commit a525a67a (`git show --cc`: only CHANGELOG adjacent entries, resolved correctly, no code touched). No leaked ids/tokens/paths; notices are English; RPA path unchanged (`review_window` never set there). Local tests: test_acl1784_api_review_window, test_acl1603_stable_slots, test_acl1761_*, test_acl1614_cancel_hung_job, test_acl1812_warm_sessions — 404 passed.

BLOCKING finding B1 — the slot is released while a profile the job started is still running, and the panel says the opposite.

In `_run_api`, `settled = clean or not wrote` drives both `review_window = not settled` (which makes `_run_job_inner` call `_slots.release` instead of `_slots.keep`) and the notice. But `ApiPublisher.finish_job` can still return "" (profile left open) for a job-started profile even when `clean=True`:
- `self.cancelled()` — user pressed Stop before the first write (cancel_job intentionally leaves the Multilogin window open, ACL-1614);
- `_keep_profiles_open()` — owner switch ACL_KEEP_PROFILES_OPEN;
- `self.dry_run` — finish_job forces clean=False (dry_run=1 jobs are reachable from the publish endpoint);
- `_stop_profile` raised (stop failure).
In all of these, wrote=False → settled=True → review_window=False → the slot is freed, yet the Mimic window the job started keeps running. That is exactly the hazard ACL-1603 guards against (queue launching extra Mimics over open windows; with cap 1 a second profile starts while the first is still open). The panel then shows API_NO_WRITE_NOTICE "the profile is not kept open for review", which is false. The Stop-before-first-write case also misses the Issue spec ("stops before the first write" → close our tab, release the slot, stop the profile if the job started it): the profile is neither stopped nor counted.

Required fix (either is acceptable, keep it small):
(a) Release the slot only when the profile is actually not left open by the job: `outcome == "closed"` OR the job did not start the profile (user-opened — spec says release in that case). If a job-started profile stays open for any other reason (cancel, keep-open switch, dry run, stop failure), keep the slot as before and do not show the "not kept open" notice (show an accurate one or none). And/or
(b) For a no-write stop, let finish_job stop the job-started profile despite `cancelled()` (spec), and still fall back to (a) when stopping did not happen.
Expose what you need from ApiPublisher read-only (e.g. a `started_profile` property from `self._opened.started_now`) rather than reaching into privates.

Tests to add (fakes; the current FakePublisher.finish_job does not model cancel/keep-open/dry-run/stop-failure, so it cannot catch this): Stop before the first write on a job-started profile; ACL_KEEP_PROFILES_OPEN=1 with a clean no-write or clean job on a job-started profile; finish_job returning "" for a job-started profile — each must either close the profile or keep the slot, and the notice must match the real state. Prefer driving the real `ApiPublisher.finish_job` with a faked `_opened`/`_stop_profile` for at least one case.

Non-blocking notes:
- `wrote` falls back to True on an exception — good (conservative).
- GraphError rejections count as writes (`GraphClient.writes` increments before POST), so a Meta-refused write keeps the window — conservative, acceptable.
- CI on a525a67a: all test/installer/descriptor checks green; `tracker-link` failed because it ran before handoff ("move it to Review before a ready PR") — rerun it on the next head.
- Owner live check (panel notice on the test dashboard) can follow separately as the Issue allows.

Lane kept (--keep-lane); I will review the fix delta.

1079.title: Adopt isolated manual verification completion support
1079.body:
## Description

Adopt the reviewed shared support that lets an actually verified, isolated manual process task finish without publishing an unchanged ACL installer. Preserve ACL application behavior, its local workflow safeguards and all other developers' ownership/history. Then validate that the adopted native client supports the real ACL-2071 completion; recording its separate supplemental receipt remains tied to the original task and genuine independent assessment.

## Specifications

Owner authorization: complete the process-completion fix end to end, with a compatible shared release and separately reviewed ACL adoption. Use existing schema3 capacity and preserve incumbent claims; no ownership exception or migration is requested. Current published selections are Master1.7.2 at4f148cbbbc2c9c65a7fdebba9b37551f91566e04 and Tracker3.9.2 at3d32586d72e4621f70d56d35f1e199a19fa13b00. Targets are independently reviewed, genuinely published Master1.8.0 at fddcdd0d60db2e14cce0a53e6af23e12356c3bc7 (v1.8.0, release420144866) and Tracker3.10.0 at e71c9829247e60d79031dbb1bb038896fcedf4cc (v3.10.0, release420140493). Actual-main checks and clean immutable no-override portable3.9 pair39691739580 passed.

Related work: TT194/PR195 and MR77 provide the compatible support. ACL2069/PR1070 belongs to the original developer with its own reserved3.9.4/1.7.3 scope; preserve that source, owner and original acceptance. This task adopts the distinct isolated_verification1 capability and does not silently complete or supersede2069.

Scope: use the maintained three-way standard upgrade against actual published official sources; inspect every local conflict. Only canonical separated process support, precise standard/engine pins, generated selected navigation/templates and relevant repository process knowledge may change. Preserve ACL's guarded scripts/acl_task_tracker.py, .workflow/adoption.json, project-specific instructions, schema3 execution with five workers/five source reviewers/batch5, disabled Stage choice, delivery target/checks/authorization, native status/ID/history policies and all state/ownership. Do not activate optional completion/context/retry/pause policies, seize foreign slots, rewrite frozen tasks, add a controller or publish an unchanged product.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Exact stable Master/Tracker releases, immutable commits and complete trusted export closure are verified; maintained upgrade preserves all local controls and non-pin selections.
- [ ] Whole product/source/configuration/build/install/update/publication scope is independently assessed; unchanged product installer is not requested for a genuinely canonical process-only support batch. Existing genuine product publication requests remain unchanged.
- [ ] Required source/main/process/descriptor and relevant shared delivery-tool regressions pass on the exact candidate; current independent source and combined reviews bind complete original scope/proof.
- [ ] Normal old-pin source approval and frozen integration admission are used under real ownership, when the integration slot is available. Actual main includes the complete reviewed scope without a product delivery request; the existing native completion procedure remains required.
- [ ] Fresh guarded client and deployed compatible reader validate adopted selections, unchanged incumbent owners/policies/history, and supported ACL2071 preview. Actual ACL2071 supplemental completion is verified separately against its original acceptance and official successful Windows run.

Checks: project descriptor and tracker-link/process admission, affected canonical support/upgrade/guard/delivery-governance regressions, exact immutable diff inspection and actual native/public readback. Full required CI is not waived. Product/runtime verification is required only if actual changes or indirect consumption invalidate the reviewed process-only proof.

Handoff: owner-selected support adoption, not started by Issue creation alone. Actual current main64e73a1e and old pins were reread. Read-only maintained upgrade stopped at two genuine local text conflicts in delivery-check.yml and VERIFICATION.md without writing; resolve explicitly preserving ACL master push/draft validation and stronger verification guidance. Shared service deployment awaits a separate concrete security approval; prepare only under the currently adopted old client. No new isolated receipt writer may activate ahead of the deployed reader. Source owner must verify actual available capacity and real In Progress before edits.

### Blockers from round 2: fixed
1. **Targeting reads.** `estimate_targeting_reads` = min(90, 6 + 6 × distinct terms and parts across all sets) is added to the per-campaign budget. The write-refusal threshold stays at 250, and the env ceiling is 250+90. I reran my FakeMeta repro (10 sets × 3 ads × 3 work-position terms, cold cache): budget 330, 252 calls used, success. With 4 terms per set the resolver cap is hit and the run is refused before any write ("press Check plan again"); this is 1771 behaviour. 2 sets × 3 terms: success.
2. **ACL-1891.** `_prepare` refuses before the first write when `chunk_calls + estimate_create_calls(plan) > budget`. Check plan (`writing=False`) keeps the old reserve. The 1891 test is rewritten and a new test is added; the 1891 suite passes.

### Remaining notes (non-blocking, no re-review needed)
- **Remaining-budget comment is inaccurate.** The comments say "if writes don't fit after the reads, `_prepare` refuses before the first write". The code only checks when there are large-video chunks. For non-video plans, the targeting reserve is the only guard. One edge: the resolver is shared across campaigns of one job, and its job cap is cumulative (`len(_results)`), so a later campaign can in theory read more than its own reserve. Cheap hardening for a follow-up: an unconditional `client.max_calls - client.calls < estimate_create_calls(plan)` refusal at the end of `_prepare` when writing.
- **The concurrent-confirm test failure is not a lock race.** The 1771 test `test_concurrent_confirms_do_not_lose_entries` (11 == 12 under load) passes in my full group run and in 150 extra 12-thread loops. `ConfirmedStore.put` holds `_STORE_LOCK` around read → modify → atomic replace, so in-process writes are serialized. The likely cause is a transient Windows file-sharing error (AV/indexer) on `os.replace` or `_read`.
